title: Toward Recursive Self-Improvement in Physical AI

details.title: Toward Recursive Self-Improvement in Physical AI
details.abstract: Toward Recursive Self-Improvement in Physical AI Recursive self-improvement (RSI) asks for more than a better robot: the process that produces improvements should itself get better. Digital agents already rewrite their own code and check each version against executable tests. But what does it take to carry these mechanisms into the physical world, where feedback is partial, trials are costly, and some mistakes cannot be undone? What the paper covers: 🧭 A ladder of claims : behavioral improvement → later-learning benefit → procedure improvement → recursion. Each step is defined by the comparison that would establish it. 🤖 Where improvement lands : policies, world models, external knowledge (skills, code, memory), the learning procedure, and the improver that revises it. 🔁 When gains carry forward : four conditions. Feedback addresses the remaining need, the receiving component can use the change, the change stays useful under task or hardware shift, and practice remains safe and affordable. 📍 Where the field stands : existing robot studies show behavioral improvement, later-learning benefits, and procedure improvement, but none yet isolates a gain attributable to recursion. 🧪 What's still open : fair tests the system can't overfit to, gains that keep stacking up, safe practice while the procedure changes, and what a first real demo of physical RSI would need to show. 🌐 Project page: https://physical2rsi.github.io/ 💻 Paper list: https://github.com/Physical2RSI/Awesome-Physical2RSI Feedback and pointers to work we missed are very welcome!

title: Deep Fusion Memory: A Chunk-Level Parametric Memory for Large Language Models

details.title: Deep Fusion Memory: A Chunk-Level Parametric Memory for Large Language Models
details.abstract: We introduce Deep Fusion Memory (DFM) , a chunk-level parametric memory architecture that enables LLMs to incorporate external knowledge without retrieval at inference time. DFM introduces two key ideas: Efficient memory construction: A causal memory predictor learns from retrieved chunk embeddings, reducing retrieval queries by 32× and retrieved items by 2048× during training data construction. Deep memory fusion: Predicted memory is integrated into intermediate hidden states through gated cross-attention, while keeping the LLM backbone frozen. Experiments demonstrate consistent improvements across knowledge-intensive QA and domain adaptation tasks. We hope this work offers a scalable and efficient direction for equipping LLMs with external parametric memory. Feedback and discussions are welcome!

title: What Generation Knows: Unlocking Fine-Grained Understanding in Unified Multimodal Models

details.title: What Generation Knows: Unlocking Fine-Grained Understanding in Unified Multimodal Models
details.abstract: 🚀 We are excited to share our latest work: "What Generation Knows: Unlocking Fine-Grained Understanding in Unified Multimodal Models" ! Unified multimodal models (UMMs) can generate images with rich visual details. But can the internal representations underlying their generation capabilities also help improve fine-grained multimodal understanding? Existing generation-assisted understanding methods primarily rely on generative supervision or explicitly generated intermediate outputs, while the potential of native generation-side representations remains largely unexplored. We aim to investigate whether these representations can be leveraged to enhance fine-grained visual understanding. To this end, we systematically investigate the visual representations of generation and understanding pathways in UMMs. Building on our findings, we introduce GAFU (Generation-Assisted Fine-grained Understanding) , a post-training framework that directly leverages native generation-side representations to enhance fine-grained visual understanding. 🔑 Key Highlights 🔍 Systematic Investigation: We systematically compare generation-side and understanding-side representations across six UMMs, revealing key properties in fine-grained semantic sensitivity, representational complementarity, and spatial dependence . Our findings show that generation-side representations are more sensitive to fine-grained semantic changes and capture visual variations that are less effectively reflected in understanding-side representations, with these advantages closely tied to spatial organization. 🧩 GAFU Framework: We propose a post-training framework that leverages native generation-side representations without requiring explicit image generation at inference. GAFU compresses and aligns generation-side features into compact G tokens , enables task-conditioned retrieval and injection of complementary information, and incorporates pairwise preference learning to encourage effective utilization of generation-side representations. 📈 Extensive Experimental Validation: We evaluate GAFU across three unified multimodal architectures (BAGEL, Janus-Pro, and Lance) and five benchmarks covering general, spatial, and domain-specific understanding. GAFU consistently outperforms matched-data SFT baselines across all 15 model–benchmark combinations , achieving  up to 20.00%, 17.94%, and 8.62% relative improvements on VStar-Bench, OmniSpatial, and VSR-Bench, respectively. Our findings demonstrate that the generation capabilities of UMMs are valuable not only for producing visual content but also for providing complementary representations that enhance fine-grained visual understanding, opening up new opportunities for synergy between understanding and generation. 📄 Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23987 💻 Code: https://github.com/LRuca/GAFU We welcome feedback and discussions!

title: Self-Distilling Future Video Representations for World Action Models

details.title: Self-Distilling Future Video Representations for World Action Models
details.abstract: We introduce FRED , a framework that trains World Action Models (WAMs) to generate better future video representations in a single denoising step, by self-distilling from noisy ground-truth futures and conditioning on short history observations. FRED outperforms competing WAMs across real-world manipulation, with especially large gains on long-horizon and out-of-domain tasks. On robot tasks demonstrated only in human videos, it reaches 50.0% success rate vs. 19.4% for the best competing WAM. 🤗 Models: https://huggingface.co/collections/FRED-AGI-LAB/fred-6adad8ae754754e2f2f1afa7

title: LaLa-World: Scaling Latent World Models with Natural Language Actions

details.title: LaLa-World: Scaling Latent World Models with Natural Language Actions
details.abstract: TL;DR A La nguage-conditioned La tent World model ( LaLa-World ) uses natural language as a shared action interface to learn from simulation, robotics, images, and videos. It predicts future visual representations for efficient planning across domains and can be fine-tuned into LaLa-Policy , which jointly predicts robot actions and future representations. Key results: One LaLa-World predictor trained across domains beats per-domain LWMs on average MPC planning performance Adding image/video data further improves planning and robustness to action phrasing vs. an RAEv2-based video generation baseline: comparable planning with 6× less training cost and 13.9× faster planning LaLa-Policy , initialized from LaLa-World, is competitive with Cosmos Policy on LIBERO and RoboCasa with up to 5.5× faster inference Project page: https://june-page.github.io/lala-world/ Code: https://github.com/junha1125/LaLa-World alphaXiv: https://www.alphaxiv.org/abs/2610.27851 arXiv: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.27851 Presentation: https://june-page.github.io/lala-world-slides/

title: FilmFlow: Agentic System for 3D Virtual Film Cinematography

details.title: FilmFlow: Agentic System for 3D Virtual Film Cinematography
details.abstract: Complex camera motion is central to visual storytelling, yet translating cinematographic intent into controllable, executable camera trajectories remains challenging. We introduce FilmFlow, an agentic framework that converts natural-language instructions or reference videos into explicit camera trajectories for dynamic 3D environments. To generate these trajectories, a Director agent constructs executable camera plans by composing high-level motions from concurrent atomic operations that jointly control translation, rotation, and framing. The Director is supported by three specialized agents: an Interpreter that extracts scene-grounded cinematographic intent, a Scout that selects initial viewpoints, and a Critic that evaluates rendered results and provides visual feedback for iterative plan refinement. We also introduce CinemaBench, comprising 150 Blender scenes from self-created and licensed sources, with five camera instructions per scene for 750 text-directed tasks and 60 reference videos associated with a subset of scenes. CinemaBench supports evaluation of both text-directed camera generation and video reference-directed camera generation. Across a diverse set of evaluated baselines, FilmFlow achieves the strongest benchmark performance and the highest user preference, demonstrating effective spatial reasoning, temporal coordination, and visual composition for executable 3D cinematography.

title: Policy-Mask: Budget-Aware Adaptation of Diffusion Features to Discriminative Tasks

details.title: Policy-Mask: Budget-Aware Adaptation of Diffusion Features to Discriminative Tasks
details.abstract: TLDR: Policy-Mask trains a REINFORCE policy that jointly picks the timestep, layer, and exactly b channels of a frozen diffusion model, then distills the selected features into a student that runs without the teacher. At 128 of 1280 channels, it beats full-width features from a fixed (t, l) by 1.2–1.6 mIoU on four segmentation benchmarks and outperforms RepFusion.

title: Meta Expert: Cross-Layer Expert Sharing for Storage- and Retrieval-Efficient MoE

details.title: Meta Expert: Cross-Layer Expert Sharing for Storage- and Retrieval-Efficient MoE
details.abstract: A comparison between the Vanilla and Meta-Expert models shows that, when trained under the optimal settings of the Vanilla model at varying depths and scales, models with Meta Experts achieve loss comparable to the Vanilla baselines while using only 70–80% as many experts, or 75–90% as many parameters. Notably, the savings in both experts and parameters grow as the models become deeper and larger, demonstrating the favorable scalability of Meta Experts. The proposed method has been scaled up in Intern-S2-Mobius, which is available at https://github.com/InternLM/Intern-S2-Mobius and https://huggingface.co/internlm/Intern-S2-Mobius .

title: Code2Video-Compass: A Comprehensive Benchmark for General-Purpose Code-Based Video Generation across T2V, I2V, and V2V

details.title: Code2Video-Compass: A Comprehensive Benchmark for General-Purpose Code-Based Video Generation across T2V, I2V, and V2V
details.abstract: We introduce Code2Video-Compass, a comprehensive benchmark for general-purpose code-based video generation across text-to-video, image-to-video, and video-to-video settings. The benchmark comprises 2,104 tasks spanning 10 categories and 24 subtypes, covering scene construction, dynamic animation, and state dependency. We evaluate 15 MLLMs using complementary objective metrics and MLLM-based judgments, revealing substantial performance gaps across input settings and task complexities, as well as a disconnect between visual quality and execution reliability. We welcome feedback and discussion!

title: RLSplat: Resource-Linear Budget Control for Feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting

details.title: RLSplat: Resource-Linear Budget Control for Feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting
details.abstract: We present RLSplat , a feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting method that enables resource-aware inference through direct Gaussian budget control. By generating exactly the requested number of Gaussians, RLSplat allows users to adapt inference cost to their available computational resources. Unlike existing methods that generate an oversized Gaussian representation and prune it afterward, RLSplat directly generates a representation within the target budget. In zero-shot evaluations, it outperforms prior budget-controllable methods across the tested budgets, achieving up to 4.1× faster inference and 9.6× lower peak memory in low-budget settings.

title: Heartbeat Thinking: Speculative Reasoning and Tool Execution While Listening in Realtime Voice Agents

details.title: Heartbeat Thinking: Speculative Reasoning and Tool Execution While Listening in Realtime Voice Agents
details.abstract: Tool-using voice agents often leave users waiting after speech ends, even when actionable information arrives earlier in the request. Speculative approaches begin work during speech, but chunk-bounded or interrupt-on-update generation can truncate a tool call before its arguments are complete. This couples computation time to speech updates, limiting useful work completed in advance. We introduce Heartbeat Thinking, which handles updated input through new Thinker invocations while allowing ongoing invocations and dispatched tools to finish. Periodic invocations read the latest partial transcript and a shared record of completed reasoning and tool results. These results help resolve missing arguments and initiate dependent calls, allowing preparation to progress across speech updates. Across SpeechFCEval, FDBench v3, and AudioCRAG, Heartbeat improves aggregate speculative tool coverage or retrieval reuse over a SHANKS-style windowed baseline, with benchmark-dependent effects on final task quality. On FDBench v3, it increases tool coverage by 16 percentage points and reduces mean final-response latency by 36.4%. The results show that heartbeat thinking paradigm preserving ongoing computation during speech can turn listening time into reusable preparation for faster and more capable voice-agent responses.

title: Agent Mosaic: Recognizing Confidentiality Leaks in Agentic LLM Systems

details.title: Agent Mosaic: Recognizing Confidentiality Leaks in Agentic LLM Systems
details.abstract: We introduce Agent Mosaic, a study of confidentiality leaks in LLM agents where combining individually accessible information reveals sensitive conclusions. Through evaluations across simulated and live agents, we show that such leaks occur even under benign queries and persist despite explicit safeguards. Benchmark dataset and code TBP.

title: RouteWeaver: Weaving Mode Selection and Execution into Unified LLM Routing

details.title: RouteWeaver: Weaving Mode Selection and Execution into Unified LLM Routing
details.abstract: LLM routing dynamically selects and coordinates heterogeneous language models across diverse tasks. However, existing approaches are largely built around a predefined execution paradigm, such as single-round, multi-round, or agentic routing, which fixes how model calls are organized and limits adaptation to different query needs. We propose RouteWeaver, a unified routing framework that integrates these routing modes within a single LLM policy, jointly learning which mode to use and how to select models within that mode. To jointly optimize mode selection and within-mode execution, we develop COMET-GRPO (COordinated Mode–Execution Training), which decouples the trajectory-level advantage into separate signals for mode selection and within-mode execution, enabling more targeted credit assignment to each decision level. We further introduce progressive exploration, which gradually shifts training from externally assigned modes to autonomous selection, so that the router first learns how to execute each mode before deciding when to use it. We evaluate RouteWeaver across mathematics, coding, knowledge, logical reasoning, and factual recall. RouteWeaver achieves an average accuracy of 61.4%, an 11.03% relative improvement over the strongest baseline, and outperforms all compared baselines in each of the five domains. Ablations show that both COMET-GRPO and progressive exploration are important for adaptive routing; without progressive exploration, the routing policy collapses entirely to single-round execution.

title: Is Complex Agentic Memory Always Needed? Naive RAG Is Stronger Than We Thought

details.title: Is Complex Agentic Memory Always Needed? Naive RAG Is Stronger Than We Thought
details.abstract: RAW-RAG challenges the necessity of complex agentic memory for long-term conversation understanding. By combining dense retrieval and reranking over raw history, it ranks first among compared memory systems in six of seven settings across four benchmarks. Its analyses highlight evidence coverage and relational completeness as key drivers of performance, establishing naive RAG as an essential baseline.

title: Cola2: Co-Adaptive Hierarchical Language Modeling with Continuous Semantic Compression and Balanced Discrete Generation

details.title: Cola2: Co-Adaptive Hierarchical Language Modeling with Continuous Semantic Compression and Balanced Discrete Generation
details.abstract: Hi everyone! We’re excited to share Cola2, a follow-up to Cola that combines dynamic semantic compression with joint learning of continuous representations and discrete text generation. With a Qwen-initialized decoder, Cola2 surpasses Llama-3-8B on HellaSwag and StoryCloze after just 346B additional training tokens, while still unconverged. We plan to open-source the 8B model in the coming weeks. Feedback and discussion are very welcome! Project page: https://hongcanguo.github.io/Cola2/

title: Different Tasks, Different Timesteps: Temporal Task-Aware Quantization for Diffusion Language Models

details.title: Different Tasks, Different Timesteps: Temporal Task-Aware Quantization for Diffusion Language Models
details.abstract: Excited to share our new paper: Different Tasks, Different Timesteps: Temporal Task-Aware Quantization for Diffusion Language Models! 🚀 We reveal that quantization sensitivity is both task and time-dependent , with different downstream tasks exhibiting distinct precision requirements across denoising steps. Building on this finding, we introduce T²Quant , a mixed-precision framework that: 🔍 Predicts precision sensitivity using only a few unlabeled calibration prompts. ⚙️ Allocates activation precision across denoising steps under a fixed bit-width budget. 📈 Improves existing quantization methods by up to 6.7 percentage points , without increasing the average precision budget. Evaluated across 3 diffusion language models and 6 benchmarks. 📄 Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.31198 We welcome feedback, questions, and discussions!

title: RTAformer: Relation-Transition-Aware Transformer for Video Scene Graph Generation

details.title: RTAformer: Relation-Transition-Aware Transformer for Video Scene Graph Generation
details.abstract: We introduce RTAformer , accepted at ACCV 2026, for Video Scene Graph Generation (VidSGG). Existing temporal models often retain outdated relation predictions even after the underlying relationships change. We identify this failure mode as Relational Semantic Inertia . RTAformer addresses this issue by disentangling entity persistence from relation dynamics, using calibrated relation-query differences to guide predicate updates and cross-frame instance alignment to stabilize temporal representations. Experiments on Action Genome demonstrate improved performance, with particularly strong gains on relation-transition frames under matched-backbone comparisons. Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20091 Code (coming soon): https://github.com/sejong-rcv/RTAformer

title: Verus-Insight: Towards Explainable Artifact Detection in AI-Generated Videos

details.title: Verus-Insight: Towards Explainable Artifact Detection in AI-Generated Videos
details.abstract: Recent advances in video generation have made synthetic videos increasingly realistic, placing greater demands on reliable AI-generated video detection. Existing artifact-based detectors typically identify generation artifacts as evidence for source prediction, yet they may either fail to recognize subtle artifacts or reach the correct source decision without faithfully identifying the evidence underlying it. In this work, we systematically investigate how to design and train effective artifact detectors and formulate artifact detection as a structured process comprising three complementary capabilities: Inspection Planning, which determines what should be examined; Evidence Verification, which verifies whether the inspected content exhibits genuine generation artifacts; and Evidence Aggregation, which integrates the verified evidence into the final source decision. Building on this formulation, we introduce Verus-Insight, trained with human-anchored full-process supervision and progressive capability training to strengthen both fine-grained artifact detection and video-level detection. We further introduce Verus-Bench, a benchmark with fine-grained human annotations of perceptible artifacts for evaluating artifact detection. Extensive experiments across diverse benchmarks demonstrate that Verus-Insight achieves strong performance in both fine-grained artifact analysis and AI-generated video detection, with substantial gains in recovering human-perceived artifacts. Further analyses reveal that the three capabilities are complementary yet distinct, and that Verus-Insight more reliably converts relevant inspection targets into supported artifact evidence without increasing spurious artifact claims.

title: Rethinking Sequence Compression with Test-time Regression

details.title: Rethinking Sequence Compression with Test-time Regression
details.abstract: Hi everyone! We introduce TTR-Compressor, a superior and fully practical alternative to standard pooling and projection-based compression. It shows strong empirical gains both as a compressor for block-wise sparse attention in efficient LLMs and as a VL projector (merger) in MLLMs. Beyond that, it opens up many exciting applications to explore: temporal compression for video/audio, training natively efficient ViTs from scratch, depth-wise compression for better depth scaling...

title: AnyGameRenderer: Entity-Consistent Generative Rendering Across Games and an Entity-Level Benchmark

details.title: AnyGameRenderer: Entity-Consistent Generative Rendering Across Games and an Entity-Level Benchmark
details.abstract: AI coding agents can now build small playable games in minutes, but the results usually look like programmer art: gray blockouts, colored geometric primitives, and flat semantic blobs. We present AnyGameRenderer, a video-to-video generative renderer that turns such footage into high-quality visuals with characters, motion detail, and effects. Throughout, it keeps the layout, camera, and every entity's position and timing intact. Our AnyGameRenderer generalizes across a wide range of genres that agents build, such as tower defense, auto-battlers, top-down survivors, turn-based battles, kart racing, and crowd runners. AnyGameRenderer takes plain video as its game-state input, with no complex representations such as engine G-buffers, per-object class labels, or low-poly proxies. Gray blockouts, colored primitives, semantic maps, and wireframes all work as input. It also preserves entity correspondence: group counts stay correct, and entities appear and disappear on the right frame. We implement AnyGameRenderer by LoRA fine-tuning MiniMax-H3 ref2va, a 33B reference-video-conditioned video generation model. Training uses ∼10k paired clips from three sources: (i) multi-stream rendering data from 38 agent-made games exported from GEAR, an AI game-creation tool; (ii) two-stream rendering data from Unreal Engine, with programmatically controlled crowds, count changes, and entity scales; and (iii) real gameplay recordings, with pairs reconstructed via 3D-box detection. To evaluate the entity correspondence, we propose an entity-level benchmark of 59 held-out cases with 753 entities, scored against ground-truth boxes. Compared with the base model, AnyGameRenderer better preserves entity correspondence: temporal match rises from 50.9% to 62.9%, missed count changes fall from 34.7% to 21.3%, and fewer entities are hallucinated or left unrendered.

title: AgentVQA: A Unified Benchmark for Agentic Visual Understanding

details.title: AgentVQA: A Unified Benchmark for Agentic Visual Understanding
details.abstract: AgentVQA is an offline benchmark for evaluating visual understanding in realistic agentic scenarios, without the cost of running agents in interactive environments. It brings together 1,000 human-verified examples from 23 datasets across five domains: web agents, robotics, egocentric videos, games, and spatial planning. Our evaluation of 22 VLMs reveals substantial limitations in visual grounding, motion understanding, state tracking, and spatial reasoning. Importantly, model rankings on AgentVQA also align with corresponding online evaluations, supporting its use as a scalable alternative for assessing agentic visual understanding.

title: MolLean: A Process-Verifiable Language for Chemical Reasoning

details.title: MolLean: A Process-Verifiable Language for Chemical Reasoning
details.abstract: MolLean turns chemical reasoning into executable, checked steps. Direct chain-of-thought can miscount atoms, invent functional groups, or claim a property improved without measuring it. MolLean ties declared edits and claims to an explicit molecular state. The video illustrates four examples from the paper: ethanol-to-1-propanol editing, an exact 25-carbon constraint, QED optimization with measured feedback, and an interactive MolLean-MCP episode where a rejected phenyl attachment leaves the molecule unchanged and guides the next successful action. Across 8,800 matched examples covering 12 chemical task types, whole-trace refinement improves over direct CoT on all 12 with Qwen3.6-27B. Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20459 Project preview: https://github.com/phenixace/Open-MolLean Code release is planned.

title: BrickWright: Agentic Creation of Physically Feasible Brick Builds

details.title: BrickWright: Agentic Creation of Physically Feasible Brick Builds
details.abstract: BrickWright enables pre-trained coding agents to generate high-fidelity, physically feasible LEGO® builds from text or image prompts. Its key idea: Give agents a programmatic toolkit for creating and validating brick builds.

title: RIDAR: Safeguarding Research Integrity in Autonomous Research Agents via Automated Detection and Runtime Intervention

details.title: RIDAR: Safeguarding Research Integrity in Autonomous Research Agents via Automated Detection and Runtime Intervention
details.abstract: Autonomous research agents are increasingly used to automate large portions of scientific research, yet they are prone to research integrity violations (RIVs): behaviors that compromise the validity, reproducibility, or faithfulness of the research process. We present RIDAR, a framework for automated RIV detection and runtime intervention. First, we introduce RIVT, a comprehensive taxonomy of 14 RIV types spanning the full research lifecycle. Building on RIVT, we present RIDAR-post-hoc, a framework to detect RIVs within agent trajectories. RIDAR-post-hoc achieves 85.2% F1 performance on RIV-Gold, a benchmark for RIV detection with 60 expert-annotated trajectories. Applying RIDAR-post-hoc to RIV-Wild, a dataset of 300 agent trajectories across 50 distinct research tasks, we detect 3,964 RIV instances in 99.7% of trajectories, revealing the prevalence of RIVs in current agents. Finally, we present RIDAR-runtime, a framework for dynamically detecting and correcting RIVs during agent runtime. RIDAR-runtime effectively reduces agent RIVs remaining at task completion by 36.8%. We will release our code and data to facilitate future research.

title: F2G-Pose: Geometry-Aware Foundation Feature Lifting for Direct RGB-D Category-Level Object Pose Estimation

details.title: F2G-Pose: Geometry-Aware Foundation Feature Lifting for Direct RGB-D Category-Level Object Pose Estimation
details.abstract: We’re sharing F2G-Pose, accepted at NeurIPS 2026! From a single segmented RGB-D observation, it predicts category-level 6D object pose, metric size, and a completed shape in the camera frame in one forward pass. It lifts frozen foundation visual features into 3D and fuses them with local geometry through a Mixture-of-Experts Transformer. No instance-specific CAD models or reference views are required. The paper reports 28 FPS for pose-only model inference under its benchmark protocol. Code, pretrained weights, and a 90-second demo are available. Happy to discuss the method and results! Pretrained weights: https://huggingface.co/J3rr1/F2G-Pose

title: Inherited, Not Invented: Tracing the Provenance of Wait in Reasoning Models

details.title: Inherited, Not Invented: Tracing the Provenance of Wait in Reasoning Models
details.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) is credited with teaching reasoning models to write {wait} before reconsidering a step, yet large RL accuracy gains do not require the word. This view can confuse what RL discovers with what a model inherits from its training data. We trace the word through open models' training histories, reading it with label-free indices of frequency, position, form and usage and an injected-error test, all computed from sampled outputs. We find that zero-RL almost never coins the marker: on bases that lack the word, RL raises MATH-500 accuracy substantially while {wait} stays near absent. It arrives with training data: mid-training in OLMo-3, and fine-tuning on reasoning traces installs it in most models whose base lacks it. Where the base already uses it, both released RL-Zero recipes (OLMo-3, MiMo) multiply it, whereas KL-free GRPO from the same base does not; OLMo-3's recipe wears down its form and makes it a more sensitive but more liberal alarm; RL after supervised fine-tuning barely changes it, and our GRPO recipe erases a marker seeded by fine-tuning. Finally, we show that marker frequency alone does not indicate RL-induced reasoning and caution against LLM-as-a-judge revision metrics, as automated judges can reverse human-labelled trends.

title: The LLM-Attacker: A Unified Red-Team Framework for Privacy Evaluation of Split and Distributed LLM Systems

details.title: The LLM-Attacker: A Unified Red-Team Framework for Privacy Evaluation of Split and Distributed LLM Systems
details.abstract: A split language model keeps its raw text on the client but sends the server per-token activations, and during training the server sends gradients back. Both messages can carry information about the private text. Keeping text local does not by itself show those messages reveal nothing, and privacy studies are hard to compare when they differ in attacker access, model knowledge, data, or what counts as recovery. LLM-Attack Suite's move is to make the evaluation itself inspectable, it records the conditions of an experiment, reuses the same captured messages across compatible attacks, and keeps predictions so results can be rescored independently

title: Who Takes the Lead? Model Ability and Task-Conditioned Collaboration with Humans

details.title: Who Takes the Lead? Model Ability and Task-Conditioned Collaboration with Humans
details.abstract: Hi everyone, This is Weien Li! When an AI agent asks for less human help, does that mean worse collaboration—or a sensible division of labor? We study this in a shared-control maze, varying whether the human or AI has the shorter route to a common goal. Across four models, stronger solo performance is associated with more selective human involvement: reliable maze solvers mostly act themselves when the human has no route advantage, but involve the human on roughly 80% of initial decisions when the human’s route is shorter. The takeaway: how often an agent involves a human tells only part of the story; we also need to examine when it does so. These are findings from a small, controlled study, and we’d love to hear ideas for testing this in other human–AI tasks!

title: SplatLab: Autonomous Scientific Discovery for 3DGS Research

details.title: SplatLab: Autonomous Scientific Discovery for 3DGS Research
details.abstract: What if AI could actually do scientific research, not just generate ideas or write papers? Excited to share SplatLab (NeurIPS 2026) , an autonomous AI scientist for 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS). Starting from a single prompt (or no prompt at all) SplatLab autonomously reads research papers, reproduces published methods, proposes novel improvements, implements code, runs real GPU experiments, performs ablations, and writes complete research manuscripts. Key results: 🧪 16 research manuscripts generated end-to-end without human code edits. 📈 Up to +3.78 dB PSNR over reproduced baselines in evaluated experiments. ⚡ 24–48 hours for an autonomous research run. 🔍 Verifiable science: Every reported numerical result is traced to an actual experiment log. Unlike AI systems that only propose hypotheses, SplatLab closes the loop from scientific ideas to experimentally validated discoveries. We've open-sourced the framework, generated manuscripts, and experimental records. We'd love feedback from the community!

details.title: TILDE: Teacher-in-the-Loop Distillation from Embodied Foundation Models

TILDE addresses this challenge by distilling teacher knowledge across demonstrations, student-induced rollouts, and teacher-executed recovery trajectories. At its core, AutoDAgger enables autonomous data collection by monitoring student execution and triggering teacher intervention, efficiently gathering recovery experience without human monitoring or manual control.

title: MambaAct: Efficient Mamba Action Experts for Flow-Matching Vision-Language-Action Models

details.title: MambaAct: Efficient Mamba Action Experts for Flow-Matching Vision-Language-Action Models
details.abstract: Hi everyone! 👋 We're excited to share MambaAct , an efficient action expert for flow-matching VLAs. Flow-matching VLAs like π0.5 run their action expert many times during denoising, which makes inference a bottleneck for real-time control. MambaAct keeps π0.5's pretrained vision-language encoder but replaces the transformer action expert with a compact Mamba-based one. A lightweight Context Compressor turns the VLM tokens into a compact conditioning signal, so we avoid repeated token-level cross-attention. 🚀 Key results: 10× smaller action expert 64.8% lower denoising latency on LIBERO, 58.8% on a real robot +1.08 pp mean success on LIBERO (3 seeds), with gains maintained on LIBERO-Plus and real-world tasks 💻 Code: https://github.com/giakhuyendihoc/MambaAct Weight will be released soon!

title: UserArena: Benchmarking Interactive User Simulation for Long-Horizon Shopping Agents

details.title: UserArena: Benchmarking Interactive User Simulation for Long-Horizon Shopping Agents
details.abstract: Can simulated shoppers faithfully reproduce real users’ behavior over long shopping interactions? We introduce UserArena , an interactive benchmark grounded in real-world e-commerce data: 64,729 sessions from 11,010 users , covering 566,102 items and 13 action types. Its five-level evaluation goes beyond next-action accuracy to assess sequential behavior, personalization, and outcomes. It also validates offline policy comparisons against a controlled production A/B test. We further propose On-Policy Trajectory Distillation (OPTD) , which uses trajectory-level intent to guide dense token-level teacher supervision on student-generated responses. Among the evaluated simulators, OPTD achieves the strongest overall fidelity and most closely reproduces the policy effect observed in production. 💻 Code & data: https://github.com/RecGPT-Team/UserArena 🌐 Project: https://recgpt-team.github.io/UserArena-Page

title: HiSTEVE 1.0: Harnessing Human-Interface VLA Agents for Open-World Games

details.title: HiSTEVE 1.0: Harnessing Human-Interface VLA Agents for Open-World Games
details.abstract: 🚀 We are excited to share our latest work: "HiSTEVE 1.0: Harnessing Human-Interface VLA Agents for Open-World Games" ! Can an AI agent autonomously complete long-horizon tasks in Minecraft using only visual observations and native keyboard-and-mouse controls, just like a human player? Existing Minecraft agents typically focus on either native visuomotor control without long-horizon autonomy or high-level planning that relies on environment APIs and predefined skills. To this end, we introduce HiSTEVE 1.0 , a hierarchical Vision-Language-Action (VLA) agent that integrates a capability-aware agent harness with a native-control VLA policy, enabling autonomous planning and execution in Minecraft without privileged game states or environment APIs. 🔑 Key Highlights 🧠 Capability-Aware Agent Harness: We develop a hierarchical orchestration framework that combines capability-constrained planning, structured memory, and evidence-driven execution recovery. A policy-coupled task completion detector further enables the agent to determine when to advance, recover, or replan during long-horizon execution. 🎮 Reliable Native-Interface Control: We design a VLA policy that handles both first-person gameplay and GUI interactions through native keyboard-and-mouse actions. To mitigate interference between these heterogeneous interaction regimes, we introduce regime-specific RMSNorm branches and separate mouse-movement token embeddings, together with a three-stage training strategy combining world knowledge injection, imitation learning, and reinforcement learning. 📈 Extensive Experimental Validation: HiSTEVE achieves state-of-the-art atomic-task performance, reaching 85.0% on MineStudio Bench and 37.4% average success on OpenHA. The complete agent also successfully executes long-horizon tasks such as crafting an iron pickaxe from scratch using only the human interface. 📄 Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.31162 We welcome feedback and discussions!

title: RSIHub: A Composable Framework for Agent-Evolution Methods

details.title: RSIHub: A Composable Framework for Agent-Evolution Methods
details.abstract: Hi everyone! We’re sharing RSIHub, an open-source framework for building and comparing agent-evolution methods. RSIHub lets researchers compose reusable operators to improve agent prompts, skills, tools, and orchestration, while keeping evaluation protected and candidate histories traceable. We implement AHE, Hyperagents, A-Evolve, and GEPA on shared infrastructure and evaluate them with MiniSWE and Codex on Terminal Bench 2 and τ³ Banking. Our goal is to make agent self-improvement experiments easier to reproduce, compare, and extend. We’d love feedback, contributions, and ideas for new evolution methods and benchmarks! 💻 Code: https://github.com/simple-agent-lab/RSIHub 🌐 Project: https://simpleagentlab.com/rsihub/

title: RynnUnify: Towards Unified Embodied Brain

details.title: RynnUnify: Towards Unified Embodied Brain
details.abstract: Introduction We present RynnUnify , a Mixture-of-Transformers architecture with an autoregressive Reasoner and a rectified-flow video Generator . Built on Cosmos3, RynnUnify connects embodied understanding, spatial grounding, and long-horizon visual planning through interleaved video-language reasoning. Unified Embodied Brain. RynnUnify brings embodied cognition, spatial grounding, and video generation into one architecture, connecting scene understanding with predictions of how the physical world evolves. Interleaved Visual Planning. RynnUnify alternates subtask reasoning with video prediction, using each generated outcome to plan the next step. Cross-chunk scene memory, self-forcing training, and adaptive durations support coherent visual planning over long horizons. Agentic Interleaved Thinking. An RL-trained agent learns when to answer directly and when to generate visual evidence. Through BCPO, it learns to formulate generation requests, interpret predicted outcomes, and select the reasoning path that benefits the task. Connect Prediction to Action. The World-Action Model ( WAM ) extension translates predictive world representations into robot control through joint video-action training, supporting composite manipulation tasks.

title: Every Weight Is a Path of Shared Discrete Decisions

details.title: Every Weight Is a Path of Shared Discrete Decisions
details.abstract: We introduce state trees , a new representation in which every weight is a path of discrete decisions, and decisions can be shared across weights. Quantization, pruning, low-rank factorization and weight sharing all become edits on a tree, and applying the weights reduces to shifts and additions. We hope it opens new directions in compression, efficient kernels and hardware. As a first, deliberately simple application, we build a state tree on the original weights, one node per 64 values. Every weight and every KV-cache value still decodes to its exact BF16 bits directly on the tensorcores , with no calibration and no accuracy trade-off. On Qwen3-8B (A100, vLLM): 24% fewer bits for the weights (12.1 instead of 16) and 22% for the KV cache up to 1.28× faster generation, end to end 1.49× more tokens in the KV cache at the same memory budget decode attention 1.2–2.5× faster than FlashAttention-2 on the same values

title: TenetBench: A Clause-Anchored Russian Corpus for Evaluating Language Models against Professional Codes of Ethics

details.title: TenetBench: A Clause-Anchored Russian Corpus for Evaluating Language Models against Professional Codes of Ethics
details.abstract: Preprint. TenetBench tests whether LLM-generated text conflicts with specific clauses of Russian-language professional codes, using conflicting requests paired with benign alternatives based on the same scenario. In the paper's main evaluation, each configuration was tested on 279 conflicting requests. Eleven of fourteen model and reasoning-mode configurations produced conflicting content on most requests, usually without a warning, as assessed by a frozen LLM judge. Available on Zenodo: 2,235 task pairs covering ten professional codes, 7,303 model-judge verdicts across twenty model and reasoning-mode configurations, human annotations on 1,260 request–response items, and the generation and evaluation pipeline. Data: CC BY 4.0. Code: Apache-2.0. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22678484

title: On-Policy Self-Training: Data-Free Self-Improvement in Large Language Models

details.title: On-Policy Self-Training: Data-Free Self-Improvement in Large Language Models
details.abstract: Can a language model improve itself without a single human-written question or answer? We introduce On-Policy Self-Training (OPST), which reformulates on-policy self-distillation as a self-training framework, driven by self-generated question-answer pairs and privileged reasoning demonstrations. Guided only by coarse, high-level topic descriptions, the model builds its own curriculum of queries and privileged reasoning traces, with no human-curated prompts or answers. A pseudo-verification filter keeps a problem only if the model can reproduce its answer in a fresh context and under a paraphrase. We evaluate in-domain self-improvement as well as knowledge retention on out-of-domain benchmarks when mixing generation domains, and transfer to multimodal inputs with Visual OPST. OPST improves both language and multimodal reasoning without human-curated questions or answers, and outperforms alternative training strategies.

title: DraMaze: A Multi-Agent Pipeline with Future-Aware Memory for Diverse Microdrama Script Generation

details.title: DraMaze: A Multi-Agent Pipeline with Future-Aware Memory for Diverse Microdrama Script Generation
details.abstract: The rapid growth of microdramas has increased demand for high-quality script production. Long-form microdrama script generation with LLMs requires both diverse plot progression and long-range narrative coherence. Our observations reveal that candidate continuations increasingly concentrate on fewer narrative mechanisms as generation progresses, while conventional retrieval may reinforce trope reuse and overlook historical information essential to future plots. To address these challenges, we propose DraMaze, a multi-agent pipeline that explores diverse causal paths through trope memory-guided evolutionary tree search and mutation. It further constructs a Backward Narrative Dependency Tree to organize, retain, and retrieve historical memories based on future narrative goals. We also introduce MiDramaBench, a bilingual benchmark for evaluating script logic and creative quality across different script lengths, together with causal-pattern metrics for narrative repetition and diversity. Experiments show consistent improvements across three backbone LLMs. For 60-episode scripts of up to 60k words, DraMaze reduces causal-pattern repetition by 32.1% and achieves a Logic score of 82.5, outperforming the best-performing baseline by 8.5 points.

title: FLOMSS: Generative Music Source Separation by Flow Matching

details.title: FLOMSS: Generative Music Source Separation by Flow Matching
details.abstract: FLOMSS systematically investigates flow matching for full-band stereo music source separation (MSS). Systematic design study: We investigate prediction targets, flow paths, single- vs. multi-source modeling, and mixture consistency. Optimal Transport-CFM with x-prediction provides the most balanced performance across the evaluated metrics. Beyond SDR: We evaluate MSS with signal-level, spectral, embedding-based, distributional, and subjective metrics, revealing a distributional–reconstruction trade-off: flow-matching models improve spectral and embedding-based similarity while generally sacrificing some SDR. Strong generative MSS performance: FLOMSS-S outperforms prior generative baselines on most spectral and perceptual metrics. Competitive subjective quality: Scaling to FLOMSS-M improves every reported objective metric over FLOMSS-S and ranks #2 overall in the listening test, despite its lower SDR than strong discriminative separators. These results highlight flow matching as a promising direction for generative music source separation with competitive perceptual quality.

title: MultiAgent-OPD: End-to-End Training of Hierarchical Multi-Agent Systems with On-Policy Distillation

details.title: MultiAgent-OPD: End-to-End Training of Hierarchical Multi-Agent Systems with On-Policy Distillation
details.abstract: ✨ Highlights Role-specific learning signals — MultiAgent-OPD combines local process supervision for Searchers with outcome-based reinforcement learning for the Leader and Answerer, addressing credit assignment in hierarchical multi-agent teams. Two-stage training recipe — First trains a teacher to search and summarize in a cascaded Search–Answer workflow, then transfers its expertise to Searchers during joint hierarchical training. Token-level on-policy distillation — A frozen, task-trained teacher scores student-generated queries and summaries on evolving subtask trajectories, providing fine-grained guidance for evidence acquisition and reporting. Joint training with a shared model — Leader, Searcher, and Answerer roles jointly optimize a shared language model to coordinate task decomposition, multi-wave search, and answer generation. Inference requires only the trained student. Strong performance across seven QA benchmarks — MultiAgent-OPD achieves 38.68% macro avg@4, outperforming M-GRPO like LLM Judge MAS-RL method by 4.06 percentage points and C-MAS + RL (cascaded MAS-RL method) by 2.61 points at the evaluated checkpoints.

title: MMVistaReason: Toward Open-Data and Post-Training Recipes for Multimodal Reasoning

details.title: MMVistaReason: Toward Open-Data and Post-Training Recipes for Multimodal Reasoning
details.abstract: Open multimodal reasoning models have benefited from large-scale reasoning supervision, yet reliable post-training remains challenging due to uneven data quality, inefficient supervision construction, imbalanced difficulty, and cross-domain interference. We introduce MMVistaReason (MVR), an open-data post-training recipe with three components: (1) broader capability coverage across complementary Analytical and Real-World reasoning groups, emphasizing structured reasoning versus visual perception and spatial grounding; (2) efficient SFT and RL data construction, standardizing heterogeneous open data through staged cleaning and annotation, combining difficulty-aware cascaded teacher distillation with answer-likelihood-based trajectory selection to construct MVR-SFT-528K, and applying scale-specific frontier filtering for MVR-RL-63K; and (3) specialize-then-integrate training, which trains complementary RL experts and consolidates their capabilities through multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD). Our analyses reveal a capacity-dependent interaction between supervision difficulty, trajectory quality, and model capacity: smaller students benefit more from selected supervision, while larger students are robust to trajectory variation and mixed-domain interference. Mixed-domain RL introduces benchmark-level negative transfer, whereas MOPD provides consistent capability integration, with the preferred KL direction varying across model scales. Across 15 multimodal benchmarks, MVR-4B achieves an average score of 72.8, outperforming Qwen3.5-9B (Instruct) and MMFineReason-8B while using about 70% fewer samples than MMFineReason. Scaling to 9B improves the average to 74.4, surpassing Qwen3.5-35B-A3B (Instruct). Overall, MMVistaReason demonstrates that systematic open-data construction and capacity-aware post-training provide a practical and scalable path toward reliable multimodal reasoning.

title: Building Auditable AI Text Detectors with Sparse Autoencoders

details.title: Building Auditable AI Text Detectors with Sparse Autoencoders
details.abstract: We propose DetectorScope---a pipeline that takes an arbitrary black-box AI detector and converts it into an auditable detector (i.e. one that is transparent about the features it uses to make its prediction). In our experiments we show that these auditable detectors maintain the performance of the underlying black box classifier on both in-distribution and out-of-distribution texts while exposing concrete and highly interpretable features for analysis. title: DuoLM: Fast and Effective Personalized Recommendation with Language Models

details.title: DuoLM: Fast and Effective Personalized Recommendation with Language Models
details.abstract: Introducing DuoLM DuoLM is a framework for fast, personalized recommendation with two jointly trained language models. An encoder turns item descriptions into compact representations that can be cached and reused across users. A ranker combines these representations with each user’s history and feedback to make personalized recommendations. Both models learn end to end from recommendation labels and guidance from a full-text teacher. The serving runtime makes this reuse practical: item representations stay on the GPU and are accessed through virtual token IDs, multiple candidates share history computation within each request, and CUDA Graphs reduce execution overhead. Together, the model and runtime reduce repeated work throughout the recommendation process.

title: LoCA: Enabling Multi-Modality in Geospatial Location Encoders

details.title: LoCA: Enabling Multi-Modality in Geospatial Location Encoders
details.abstract: 🌍 LoCA: Enabling Multi-Modality in Geospatial Location Encoders Location encoders such as SatCLIP and GeoCLIP turn (lat, lon) into general-purpose embeddings by contrastive alignment with satellite imagery. This paper shows why this works and what it takes to make it multimodal. Key findings 📐 Location encoders provably keep contrastive learning away from its optimum, and training image and location encoders jointly from scratch collapses the embedding covariance to very low rank. 🔁 SatCLIP-style encoders work because the frozen image encoder acts as a high-rank covariance regularizer that the location encoder folds onto. 🛰️ Extending this to multiple sensors requires a target that is co-aligned across modalities and has high effective rank. LoCA (Location Contrastive Alignment) Stage 1: Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 encoders are co-aligned with contrastive learning. Stage 2: location and metadata encoders are fitted onto them with multi-view contrastive learning. At inference, only coordinates are needed. Results: against SatCLIP, GeoCLIP, GT-Loc, AlphaEarth and Copernicus-FM on 17 tasks (land cover, wildfire, climate, geophysical, socio-economic, biodiversity), LoCA has the most task wins, ranks top-2 on 11, and wins 68.8% of pairwise comparisons against the other encoders. Its embeddings use 62% of their dimensions, compared with 35% for SatCLIP. 💻 Code and pretrained weights (coming soon): https://github.com/eleannavali/LoCA

title: Echo: Coupled Action and Task Status Signal Denoising for Vision Language Action Models

details.title: Echo: Coupled Action and Task Status Signal Denoising for Vision Language Action Models
details.abstract: Recognizing task completion and failure enables robots to stop upon success and initiate recovery or replanning after failure. Existing methods augment Vision Language Action (VLA) policies with task status signal prediction to support these execution decisions. However, learning and integrating these signals can require fine-grained supervision, external monitoring models, or complex architectural designs. Moreover, the potential of task status signals to directly guide action generation remains underexplored. We present Echo, a framework that combines task status signal learning without frame-level progress annotations with a compact design for status prediction and action generation within a single VLA. Specifically, Echo represents task status with stop and failure signals, added as two dimensions of each action chunk and denoised together with robot actions. Their combination distinguishes ongoing execution, successful completion, and failure. To learn these signals without fine-grained progress annotations, Echo constructs successful, failed, and recovery trajectories with complementary supervision properties. To enable status signal-guided action generation, Echo controls interactions between the signals and actions and denoises the signals faster than the actions. These allow later action denoising steps to condition on cleaner status estimates while preserving accurate signal prediction. Extensive real-world manipulation experiments show that Echo accurately predicts task status and consistently improves policy performance.

title: A path-following framework on fiber bundle for variational inequalities

details.title: A path-following framework on fiber bundle for variational inequalities
details.abstract: This paper presents a general-purpose path-following algorithm that solves general variational inequalities with continuous mappings and polytope domains to arbitrary precision, achieving global linear convergence: exact for nonsingular solutions, and up to any prescribed precision for singular ones. The key insight is to view the solution set of a fixed-point KKT system as a fiber bundle (the "fixed-point bundle") over the simplex, whose geometry separates motion along the base from motion along the fibers. This unifies starting point selection, path-following, and singularity avoidance: at a singular point, where existing path-following guarantees break down, the algorithm simply jumps along the fiber to a nonsingular point and continues. Experiments on 6400 random instances with dimensions up to 1024 reduce the gap below 1e-5 in every case; code and data are available at https://github.com/shb20tsinghua/FiberBundle_VI . A follow-up (arXiv:2609.16158) extends the framework to product-of-simplex domains for Nash equilibrium computation.

title: The fixed-point bundle method over product-of-simplex domains arising from game equilibria

details.title: The fixed-point bundle method over product-of-simplex domains arising from game equilibria
details.abstract: This paper extends the fiber-bundle path-following framework of arXiv:2606.00778 to product-of-simplex domains, so that the algorithm solves arbitrary m-player n-action general-sum games to arbitrary precision, inheriting global linear convergence: exact for nonsingular equilibria, and up to any prescribed precision for singular ones. Rather than re-proving convergence, we construct an equivalent variational inequality on a single simplex and establish a fiber bundle isomorphism between the two frameworks, complemented by a slice-extension argument that transfers all guarantees from the original paper. The resulting composite bundle also permits jumps along fibers that avoid singular points, where existing path-following guarantees would otherwise break down. Experiments on 5600 random instances with dimensions ranging from 2-player 128-action to 128-player 2-action reduce the gap below 1e-5 in every case; code and data are available at https://github.com/shb20tsinghua/FiberBundle_VI .

details.title: Trajectory2Gym: Decision-Grounded Compositional Interaction Synthesis for Tool-Use Agents
details.abstract: Trajectory2Gym is a framework for scaling tool-use agents through compositional coverage and decision-grounded supervision. It constructs executable interactions that capture multi-step dependencies and trains agents on decisions supported by their visible interaction history. Across five Qwen3 model scales, Trajectory2Gym consistently improves performance on τ-bench, τ²-bench, and BFCL, achieving +16.9 to +29.8 percentage points in the average benchmark score.

title: StreamVibe: Proactive Video Agents for Evolving User Intent

details.title: StreamVibe: Proactive Video Agents for Evolving User Intent
details.abstract: Vision-language models are shifting from offline passive understanding toward online proactive interaction. However, prevailing methods largely rely on explicit requests while overlooking implicit user intents (e.g., “where should I click next?” when a user is navigating a website) and fail to continuously update their understanding as user intents evolve. These limitations make them less suitable for intent-aware interaction in real-world scenarios. To address these challenges, we introduce StreamVibe-Bench, a new benchmark that serves as a testbed for user intent understanding and interaction, comprising 4.1K evaluation samples and 85K training samples spanning explicit, implicit, and dynamic intents. Building on this benchmark, we develop StreamVibe-VL, a streaming proactive model that infers implicit user intents from continuous observations and dynamically adapts its interactions as these intents evolve. We further introduce StreamVibe-Harness, which maintains user intents as persistent states with flexible lifecycles through hierarchical memory, enabling it to track the latest user intents and environmental states. Our experiments reveal three key findings: (i) StreamVibe-VL preserves strong general video understanding capabilities while improving response timing and answer quality by 10.7% over existing baselines; (ii) existing proactive models remain limited in understanding user intents and determining when to respond, especially under implicit and dynamic intents; and (iii) StreamVibe-Harness further improves response consistency and adaptation during sustained interactions, resulting in a 12.3% gain in proactive interaction performance.

title: Trial by Trace: Benchmarking AI Agent Harnesses for Reliability and Failure Attribution

details.title: Trial by Trace: Benchmarking AI Agent Harnesses for Reliability and Failure Attribution
details.abstract: Task success does not always mean the agent harness worked reliably. We introduce TraceTrial-Bench, a benchmark that evaluates agent task performance and harness reliability separately, using 95 mechanism-oriented tasks across seven components: context, execution, governance, lifecycle, observability, tools, and verification. Across 4 harnesses, 9 models, and 3,420 runs, 31.1% of runs achieve task success despite failing at least one harness criterion. Our framework combines trajectory tracing, multi-source evidence, and two-layer evaluation to support auditable reliability assessment and evidence-based failure analysis. We welcome feedback from researchers and developers working on agent harnesses, evaluation, and reliability!

title: Work Agents: Systems, Capabilities, and Optimization

details.title: Work Agents: Systems, Capabilities, and Optimization
details.abstract: As foundation models evolve from information generation to digital work execution, agents are increasingly capable of completing complex tasks across tools, applications, and workflows. However, existing research lacks a unified perspective on how agents reliably accomplish delegated work. To address this gap, we present a work-centric, system-level perspective that views work agents as systems combining foundation models and runtime harnesses to execute tasks in stateful workspaces and deliver verifiable outcomes. We introduce two complementary dimensions, work persistence and work openness, to characterize working conditions, and classify digital work into five forms according to task scope and organization. Building on this framework, we identify five core capability families required for reliable work execution and examine approaches to model optimization, harness optimization, and their joint optimization. We further analyze existing evaluation methods and metrics from the perspective of work outcomes. Finally, we discuss future research directions, including sustained work delegation, adaptation to open environments, and the interaction between work execution and capability improvement. This paper provides a unified framework for understanding, optimizing, and evaluating work agents, supporting the development of systems capable of delivering reliable, verifiable, and practically valuable work outcomes.

title: Eat Your Precision: Precision Objective Mitigates Reward Hacking in Rubric-based RL

details.title: Eat Your Precision: Precision Objective Mitigates Reward Hacking in Rubric-based RL
details.abstract: Rubric-based rewards enable effective reinforcement learning on non-verifiable tasks. However, because these rewards are typically defined as a weighted measure of rubric coverage, models are trained primarily to maximize a recall objective. As a result, RL-trained models produce responses that are more complete but also more verbose and contain more unnecessary or factually incorrect content, leading them to be less preferred than responses from the base model. To address this issue, we present the FORK reward, which jointly optimizes recall and a novel precision objective, which requires each unit of a model response to be both necessary and factually correct, as measured by rubric-driven necessity credits and a factual-correctness grader, respectively. Our experimental results show that FORK outperforms existing rubric-based RL methods and achieves Pareto-optimal performance that balances rubric coverage and overall response quality. Compared to the original recall-based reward, FORK substantially improves precision and reduces response length while achieving similar rubric coverage, which leads to significantly higher win rate compared to the base policy (e.g., from 10.6% to 68.0% on RubricHub-Medical and from 22.1% to 74.1% on HealthBench).

title: Trustworthy Recursive Self-Improvement in the Era of Large Models: Foundation, Risks, Evaluation and Open Challenges

details.title: Trustworthy Recursive Self-Improvement in the Era of Large Models: Foundation, Risks, Evaluation and Open Challenges
details.abstract: AI systems built around large models increasingly use experience and feedback to make persistent changes to models, prompts, memories, tools, and workflows. Recursive self-improvement (RSI) extends this process to inductive biases and to the mechanisms that govern future updates, which can themselves be revised and reused across improvement cycles. Yet self-modification alone does not guarantee trustworthy improvement. Reported gains may reflect flawed evaluations, previously acquired capabilities may deteriorate, and compliance with behavioral constraints may weaken. Compromised artifacts or sensitive information may also persist in successor systems. Changes to improvement mechanisms may invalidate earlier verification results and make human oversight less effective. This survey presents an operational definition and process framework for RSI and organizes the requirements for trustworthy RSI into four interconnected themes: genuine and sustained improvement; behavioral constraints, alignment, and fairness; system security and privacy; and transparency and controllability. We examine these themes from three perspectives: Improvement Validity, Constraint Preservation, and Effective Oversight. This analysis covers improvement diagnosis, proposal generation, proposal evaluation, and update implementation (S1--S4), including the recursive application of these stages to improvement mechanisms (RI). We review risks, safeguards, and evaluation evidence for individual updates, effects inherited by successor systems, and revisions to improvement mechanisms, while distinguishing direct RSI findings from evidence in related systems. Finally, we examine evaluation settings, identify requirements for independent and longitudinal assessment, and discuss applications and open research problems.

title: Continual Learning Exam: Benchmarking Long-Horizon RSI and Experiential Learning in LLM Agents

details.title: Continual Learning Exam: Benchmarking Long-Horizon RSI and Experiential Learning in LLM Agents
details.abstract: 🚀 Introducing Continual Learning Exam (CLE): Benchmarking Long-Horizon RSI and Experiential Learning in LLM Agents! 🧠 Can LLM agents truly learn from experience and continuously improve over time? Most existing agent benchmarks focus on whether agents can solve individual tasks. But real-world intelligence requires more than task completion: agents should learn from past successes and failures, accumulate experience, and transfer acquired knowledge, strategies, and skills to future challenges. To bridge this gap, we introduce Continual Learning Exam (CLE), a large-scale benchmark designed to evaluate long-horizon continual learning and experience-driven self-improvement in LLM agents. 🌟 Key Highlights: 🔹 Built with 50+ domain experts, covering 120 real-world professional tasks, 600 progressive levels, and 89 occupations across 12 domains. 🔹 Realistic professional environments, featuring ~24K real-world files, 19 stateful applications, and 16K+ human-authored evaluation criteria. 🔹 Game-like Task Ladders, where agents must complete each level to unlock the next. Later levels require agents to reuse and build upon knowledge, strategies, and skills acquired through earlier experience. 📊 Key Findings: We evaluated 17 frontier agent configurations. Even the strongest system, Claude Code + Opus 5, achieves only: • 47.7% level completion rate • 23.3% full Task Ladder completion rate These results reveal a substantial gap between solving individual tasks and achieving genuine long-term continual learning. We hope CLE can serve as a realistic and verifiable benchmark to advance research on Agent Continual Learning, Memory, Skill Learning, and Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI). 💡 Beyond Task Solving: Towards Continual Learning and Experience-Driven Self-Improvement. We welcome feedback, discussions, and collaborations from the community!

title: S3AC: Stabilized, Selective, and Scalable Actor-Critic for LLM Reasoning

details.title: S3AC: Stabilized, Selective, and Scalable Actor-Critic for LLM Reasoning
details.abstract: Critic-free methods are widely used in reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) for long chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning, avoiding difficult and costly critic training. Common alternatives lack token-level credit assignment and typically rely on grouped rollouts to estimate prompt-specific baselines. A critic can address both limitations, but longCoT critic training is hindered by insufficient coverage of trajectories with diverse lengths and early gradients dominated by the newly initialized value head. We introduce S3AC (Stabilized, Selective, and Scalable Actor–Critic) for LLM reasoning, built around a practical critictraining recipe. The trained critic provides token-specific advantages and prompt-specific baselines. Using the prompt-level baseline to estimate difficulty, we propose DifficultyAware Prompt Sampling (DAPS). DAPS combines this estimate with outcome history to select prompts before generation, reducing rollout waste without offline difficulty initialization. S3AC improves group-rollout performance across dense and mixture-of-experts models from 1.5B to 397B parameters, outperforming a modern GRPO variant (GRPO-X). At 35B, it sustains single-rollout training while tested critic-free baselines deteriorate after initial gains.

title: RynnVLA-Latent: Scaling Robotic Manipulation Foundation Models with 3D-Grounded Latent Actions

details.title: RynnVLA-Latent: Scaling Robotic Manipulation Foundation Models with 3D-Grounded Latent Actions
details.abstract: Our contributions are as follows: 3D-grounded latent-action supervision. We introduce RynnLAM, which combines residual feature prediction, camera-compensated 3D-flow supervision, and camera-motion decoupling to construct continuous transition representations without native robot-action labels. Scalable VLA pretraining from heterogeneous video. We develop RynnVLA-Latent, which learns shared latent-action targets from 30.1K hours of human, robot, and simulation videos, and transfers the pretrained policy to native robot controls through embodiment-specific post-training. Representation and policy-level validation. We demonstrate control predictability through frozen-representation probes, competitive manipulation performance across simulation and real-world platforms, and improvements with increasing latent-action pretraining data.

title: ProAS: A Progress-Aware Advantage Shaping Framework for Multi-Turn Agentic Reinforcement Learning

details.title: ProAS: A Progress-Aware Advantage Shaping Framework for Multi-Turn Agentic Reinforcement Learning
details.abstract: We argue against the limitations of the traditional GRPO-type credit assignment, such as (1) the unreasonable reinforcement of unreasonable actions within the positively advantaged trajectory,  and (2) the fact that actions within the negatively advantaged trajectory are penalized with the same magnitude regardless of how much the remaining course deviates. Based on such insights, we propose ``ProAS: A Progress-Aware Advantage Shaping Framework for Multi-Turn Agentic Reinforcement Learning''.   It calibrates the GRPO-type credit assignment and results in the improvement of effectiveness and efficiency under multiple setups.

title: miniTE: Diagnosing and Bridging the Execution Gap in Native NVFP4 Reinforcement Learning

details.title: miniTE: Diagnosing and Bridging the Execution Gap in Native NVFP4 Reinforcement Learning
details.abstract: 🚀 Can we really train LLMs with native FP4 reinforcement learning — without sacrificing stability? Excited to share miniTE , our open-source framework for stable and efficient native NVFP4 (W4A4) RL! One surprising finding: Same weights + same precision ≠ same policy. Even when both the learner and rollout engine use NVFP4, subtle differences in numerical execution can introduce significant training–inference mismatch and eventually destabilize RL. With miniTE, we tackle this challenge from both numerical and systems perspectives: 🔬 Diagnose & align: Identify cross-engine execution differences and bring training–inference log-probability gaps down to ~1e-8 in our strict-alignment setting. ⚡ Make FP4 actually fast: Optimize native NVFP4 kernels, scaling, and grouped GEMMs, achieving up to 1.39× BF16 learner throughput on 8×B300 GPUs. 📈 Keep learning stable: Demonstrate long-horizon RL on Qwen3-30B-A3B with downstream performance close to BF16. Beyond the results, we're releasing the framework, kernels, diagnostics, and training recipes to make native low-bit RL easier to reproduce and extend. FP4 is not just about using fewer bits — it's about making every bit work. 🔥 📄 Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23928 💻 Details: https://infix.io/research/miniTE We'd love to hear your thoughts, feedback, and ideas for pushing low-precision RL further!

title: Extreme Compression of Per-Layer Embeddings via Cross-Layer Latent Vector Quantization

details.title: Extreme Compression of Per-Layer Embeddings via Cross-Layer Latent Vector Quantization
details.abstract: Recent work shows that increasing embedding capacity can improve language models, making it a promising direction for scaling. As more capacity goes into embedding tables, extreme compression becomes increasingly important: we want to keep the benefits of larger embeddings while fitting models into limited deployment memory. We study this in Gemma 4, where per-layer embeddings (PLE) account for 35.2% of E4B's parameters. At 100× compression, only about five bytes remain for each token–layer vector. Encoding every vector independently gives each one a tiny code and misses the opportunity to share storage across layers. Our method, OPTIC, gives each token one quantized code shared across all layers. Layer-specific affine decoders reconstruct the different PLE vectors from that shared code. We also fit the representation to its effect after the gate and output projection, so the compression objective reflects how the model actually uses the embeddings. At about 100× PLE compression, OPTIC retains 97.8% of BF16 E4B performance across seven benchmarks, compared with 66.3% for product quantization. Serving BF16 E4B directly from the compact codes reduces GPU memory by 29.7%, with at most 0.40% more wall time on an RTX 4090 with the same 1 GiB KV cache. It also works alongside backbone weight quantization. Paper · Code and method walkthrough · Released 100× PLE artifact

title: CausalAlign: Causal Alignment of Video Generation Models for Consistent Ego-Motion

details.title: CausalAlign: Causal Alignment of Video Generation Models for Consistent Ego-Motion
details.abstract: Diffusion-based video generation models (VGMs) can synthesize visually compelling content, but maintaining geometrically consistent camera ego-motion across frames remains an open problem. Camera ego-motion describes these cross-frame viewpoint changes; geometrically inconsistent future predictions can induce systematic errors in downstream action prediction. To address this problem, we propose CausalAlign, a framework combining causal diagnosis and delta-token alignment. First, we diagnose how ego-motion is represented, used, and retained within VGMs using linear probes and causal interventions. In the base model, both measures rise and then fall across denoising layers and timesteps: ego-motion is used at intermediate stages but is not retained later, a pattern we call geometric state forgetting. Second, we construct a delta-token space from a 3D foundation model and align VGM representations where ego-motion begins to fade. Delta tokens encode changes between consecutive frames, focusing supervision on motion rather than redundant static scene content. With Wan2.2 fine-tuned on DL3DV and RealEstate10K, CausalAlign preserves visual quality while improving motion accuracy, geometric consistency, and temporal smoothness. For example, it reduces geometric consistency errors by more than 20% relative to the base model. Moreover, using the fine-tuned VGM, CausalAlign improves downstream world action models (WAMs) on the RoboCasa365 benchmark. Overall, CausalAlign improves ego-motion consistency in diffusion-based VGMs and yields gains in downstream embodied models on motion-intensive tasks.

title: Joint or Per-Option? Compact Encoders for Closed-Set Decisions from 17 Million to 1 Billion Parameters

details.title: Joint or Per-Option? Compact Encoders for Closed-Set Decisions from 17 Million to 1 Billion Parameters
details.abstract: Author here. Many LM pipelines end in a closed-set decision: pick a tool, a label, a route. We asked two things: how small an encoder for this can be, and whether it should read the options jointly or one at a time. Per-option vs joint: in a three-seed study at 32M parameters, per-option scoring wins by 5.8 points of chance-corrected skill at matched optimizer steps, and by 2.8 at roughly matched compute. The advantage needs a reranker initialisation; from the raw encoder the two readers are indistinguishable. Cost: per-option needs 5–13× more encoder passes, so joint is what we released. Released models: six open joint encoders, from 17M to 1B. On 209 overlap-audited System1-Arena tasks, the 68M and 150M beat a 435M DeBERTa-v3 zero-shot classifier by 4.9 and 5.9 accuracy points. On the 145 tasks unseen in training they are at least on par with it. Latency: the 17M answers a median request in 14 ms on 16 CPU threads. A caveat we measured: reordering options changes 12–23% of the joint models' answers. Models: https://huggingface.co/collections/tardellirs/crivo-6acaa1731d71f839970f04a6 Code and results: https://github.com/tardellirs/crivo-decision-encoders Happy to answer questions!

title: Thinking-in-Bets at Test Time Reduces Sycophantic Revisions in LLM Agents

details.title: Thinking-in-Bets at Test Time Reduces Sycophantic Revisions in LLM Agents
details.abstract: Language model agents often abandon correct work when a user challenges it, yet simply telling them to stand firm makes them ignore real mistakes. Once an agent reads a complaint, it tends to discount its own earlier checks in order to agree with the user. We introduce Thinking-in-Bets, a training-free method in which an agent writes a short private record of its main claims, the checks supporting them, and its confidence before reading user feedback. When challenged, the agent consults this Claim Checklist to keep verified work intact while investigating uncertain or newly challenged parts. We evaluate five Gemini models (3.5 Flash-Lite, 3.5 Flash, 3.6 Flash, 3.8 Flash, and 4.0 Argon) across eight benchmarks: SWE-Together, SWE-Interact, and DeepSWE for software engineering, Agents' Last Exam for professional reports, Humanity's Last Exam and SycEval for academic reasoning, Vals Finance for financial analysis, and Terminal-Bench for command-line tasks. Recording claims before criticism nearly eliminates false reversals in patch review and protects passing report drafts under mistaken pushback, whereas writing the same record after reading the complaint recovers very little of the gain. In multi-turn coding, pre-reply claim records substantially reduce unnecessary file edits after mistaken complaints, and gating the record so it is written only when the agent is uncertain lowers token overhead while fixing more real bugs than the baseline. Even in non-interactive tasks without user feedback, listing the key claims in a draft and re-checking the weakest one before submission improves both answer accuracy and confidence estimates across all tested models.
