title: DialFork: Going Beyond Factuality to Evaluate Procedural Hallucination in Conversational Agents

details.title: DialFork: Going Beyond Factuality to Evaluate Procedural Hallucination in Conversational Agents
details.abstract: Ask an LLM agent to check the weather. It's polite, fluent and never says anything false... and twenty turns later you still don't have your forecast. 🌦️ That's procedural hallucination : the agent stops following the procedure it was given. Every turn looks fine on its own, so fact-checkers and per-turn quality metrics miss it. DialFork is a benchmark for catching it, with no annotation needed. We take a conversation where the agent does everything right, replay it with the same seed, and slip the agent a new instruction at some point, so the conversation "forks" 🔱. The fork position gives us labels for free: how far each fork strays and the turn where it starts straying. 36,278 English dialogues · 24 tasks · 12 domains · 4 hallucination types 3 tasks: set-to-set distance (monitoring), dialog-to-dialog distance (procedural retrieval) and turn prediction (real-time guardrails) 🤗 Dataset: https://huggingface.co/datasets/DialFork/dialfork 💻 Code & leaderboard: https://github.com/idiap/dialfork

details.title: Trust Mechanisms for Offline Generative AI at the Edge: A Connectivity-Regime Framework and an Empirical Study on a Raspberry Pi 5
details.abstract: We study what trust mechanisms do, and cost, for a fully local RAG assistant on a Raspberry Pi 5 running under network isolation (Qwen2.5 1.5B/3B/7B, 300 SQuAD 2.0 questions). Key findings: A calibrated retrieval-score gate detects out-of-corpus queries almost perfectly (AUROC 0.97) but in-topic unanswerable questions poorly (0.68). A simple deterministic output validator turns malformed outputs into explicit abstentions at no observed cost in correct answers. Signature and hash checks alone accepted 6 of 9 update attacks (rollback, replay, expiry, revoked keys, model incompatibility); layered verification rejected all 9 in about 4.5 ms. A validly signed but poisoned knowledge pack passed every check and eliminated correct answers on all 30 targets: integrity establishes provenance, not truth. Code, per-query outputs, and analysis scripts are open (DOI and GitHub links above); every table value can be regenerated with one command.

title: Assessing the CAD Capabilities of General-Purpose AI Models: A Case Study of GPT-6 Astra

details.title: Assessing the CAD Capabilities of General-Purpose AI Models: A Case Study of GPT-6 Astra
details.abstract: Can frontier AI models generate CAD models that are actually usable in engineering? Unlike evaluations centered on simplified or toy examples, our study assesses GPT-6 Astra using realistic engineering CAD models with nontrivial complexity. More importantly, we evaluate not only whether AI can generate CAD geometry, but also whether the resulting models satisfy multiple engineering usability requirements, including geometric validity, functional completeness, assembly feasibility, and parametric editability. Across CAD understanding, generation, editing, and evaluation tasks, our findings reveal an important transition: general-purpose AI models are beginning to demonstrate practical value in engineering design, while significant challenges remain in ensuring engineering reliability. The key question is no longer just whether AI can create CAD models, but whether those models can actually be used in engineering workflows. Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.24451 Project: https://qiang-zou.github.io/projects/icad-eval-report/

title: Beyond Benchmarks: Can Small Open-Weight Models Get Real Coding Work Done?

details.title: Beyond Benchmarks: Can Small Open-Weight Models Get Real Coding Work Done?
details.abstract: Most coding benchmarks measure whether a model can solve a problem. But what happens when we ask smaller open-weight models to complete real software engineering tasks? In Beyond Benchmarks , I investigate this gap through practical coding workflows, looking beyond benchmark scores to understand task completion, reliability, human intervention, and the economics of using open-weight models. The goal is not to declare a winning model, but to understand where smaller models are genuinely useful, where they struggle, and what it takes to make them effective in real development environments. I hope these findings help researchers and engineers building more practical, affordable, and accessible AI coding systems. Feedback, criticism, and independent replication are very welcome! Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.34241

title: ChronoReplay: One Answer Interface Is Not Enough for Streaming Spatial Intelligence

details.title: ChronoReplay: One Answer Interface Is Not Enough for Streaming Spatial Intelligence
details.abstract: ChronoReplay is a training framework designed to improve the spatial reasoning capabilities of streaming vision-language models (VLMs). Existing spatial VLMs often specialize in specific answer formats, such as categorical spatial relations, metric distances, or motion trajectories. This specialization, which we call interface lock-in, limits generalization across different spatial reasoning tasks. To address this challenge, ChronoReplay organizes heterogeneous spatial supervision into chronologically ordered episodes, preserves task-specific answer formats, and balances learning across supervision families. This enables a single model to learn complementary spatial capabilities while maintaining temporal consistency. Key Highlights: Unified Spatial Learning: Supports categorical, metric, and trajectory-based spatial reasoning within a single model. Chronological Replay: Preserves temporal dependencies by organizing training examples into ordered interaction episodes. Family-Balanced Training: Improves cross-task generalization by balancing heterogeneous supervision signals. Strong Benchmark Performance: Achieves consistent improvements across OVO-S-Bench, OST-Bench, and UCS-Bench, including a 13.41-point improvement on OST-Bench. Efficient Streaming Inference: Adaptive frame selection further improves performance while reducing visual processing costs. ChronoReplay demonstrates that effective streaming spatial intelligence requires preserving complementary spatial information across tasks, learning from temporally structured experiences, and selecting relevant visual evidence at inference time.

title: HABIT-Bench: Evaluating Habit Induction from Longitudinal Weak Evidence in Agent Memory

details.title: HABIT-Bench: Evaluating Habit Induction from Longitudinal Weak Evidence in Agent Memory
details.abstract: Hi everyone! I'm one of the authors of HABIT-Bench 👋 Can an agent learn your habits without being explicitly told—and know when not to apply them? Remembering a past choice is not enough. An agent needs to distinguish a recurring habit from a one-off exception, recognize when habits change, and avoid treating its own suggestions as the user's preferences. We introduce HABIT-Bench to evaluate this ability across food, finance, software, and travel. It uses synthetic user histories spanning hundreds of sessions. The tasks require agents to piece together scattered, incomplete evidence and select an appropriate action for a new request—not simply recall something the user explicitly stated. We evaluate eight memory methods with Qwen3-235B-A22B and GLM-5.3-Flash. The best memory-method configuration reaches 33.61% macro accuracy on four-choice tasks, compared with 25% for random guessing . Even when annotated evidence is provided directly, substantial errors remain: finding relevant history is only part of the challenge. Remembering what happened is not the same as understanding what should guide the next decision. 💻 Code: https://github.com/LUMIA-Group/habit-bench 🤗 Dataset: https://huggingface.co/datasets/hollyming/HABIT-Bench We'd love to hear your thoughts, discuss the findings, and see how other memory systems perform on HABIT-Bench!

title: CodeCap-Bench: Can Code Serve as a Good Video Caption?

details.title: CodeCap-Bench: Can Code Serve as a Good Video Caption?
details.abstract: Video captioning aims to preserve visual information through compact descriptions, predominantly using natural language. However, precisely expressing fine-grained spatial structures and temporal dynamics in natural language often leads to lengthy and potentially ambiguous descriptions. In this work, we explore Code as Video Caption, a paradigm where executable programs serve as a complementary representation of visual content through graphical primitives, layout rules, and functions of time. To examine whether code captions effectively preserve video information, we compare them with natural language captions on downstream question answering and video reconstruction tasks. Our results show that code captions achieve superior reasoning accuracy and reconstruction fidelity. Despite these advantages, realizing the potential of code captioning depends on whether current multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can generate faithful code captions. To systematically assess this capability, we introduce CodeCap-Bench, which comprises 323 videos spanning five categories of structured 2D content, along with fine-grained annotations and a multi-level evaluation framework. Extensive experiments reveal that while leading proprietary MLLMs demonstrate promising code captioning capabilities, they still struggle to faithfully capture complex temporal dynamics, with open-source models lagging substantially behind.

title: Can Discrete Tokens Serve as Semantically Lossless Representations of Visual Signals?

details.title: Can Discrete Tokens Serve as Semantically Lossless Representations of Visual Signals?
details.abstract: This paper investigates whether discrete visual tokens can preserve semantic information as effectively as continuous representations. It shows that reconstruction error is an unreliable indicator of multimodal understanding and identifies effective bit budget as a key performance factor. The proposed Factorized Vector Quantization (FVQ) uses complementary, fixed-dimensional projections and parallel codebooks to overcome performance saturation in existing quantizers. Experiments demonstrate that FVQ scales effectively with increasing bit budgets and matches continuous features in controlled evaluations. At industrial scale, FVQ achieves strong multimodal understanding, including fine-grained OCR, challenging the assumption that visual discretization necessarily entails semantic degradation in downstream understanding tasks.

title: ThinkWorld: World Imagination Reinforces Chain-of-Dynamics Reasoning

details.title: ThinkWorld: World Imagination Reinforces Chain-of-Dynamics Reasoning
details.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have made substantial progress in robotic manipulation, but their generalization remains constrained by the diversity and coverage of action-labeled robot demonstrations. Human videos provide much broader behavioral and environmental experience, while learning from them faces a fundamental trade-off between scalable data and explicit action grounding. We introduce ThinkWorld , a VLA learning framework that grounds action reasoning in world dynamics and strengthens it through reinforcement learning with world imagination. ThinkWorld represents each action thought as a Chain-of-Dynamics (CoD), a sequence of discrete motion tokens that captures the intermediate dynamics connecting the current world to a future state and serves as a common action representation across embodiments. We first initialize CoD with action-labeled demonstrations, then predict the future induced by each CoD and reinforce those whose predictions better match the observed outcome. This enables videos without action annotations to provide direct supervision from observed state transitions, allowing human and robot experience to refine the same reasoning space. Experiments in simulation and on real robots demonstrate effective human-to-robot transfer and strong generalization to unseen tasks and environments.

title: Can Test-Time Memory Evolution Outperform Test-Time Training for Scientific Discovery?

details.title: Can Test-Time Memory Evolution Outperform Test-Time Training for Scientific Discovery?
details.abstract: Recent test-time training (TTT) frameworks have enabled open-weight large language models (LLMs) to outperform inference-only frameworks powered by frontier models on scientific discovery tasks. However, TTT introduces additional computational cost for online weight updates during the discovery process, making computational efficiency an important consideration when scaling to larger models. This motivates us to explore an efficient test-time adaptation method for scientific discovery. We introduce Test-Time Memory Evolution (TTME), a plug-and-play test-time adaptation method, as an alternative to TTT. TTME continually updates the external memory by distilling the experience to guide subsequent discovery without updating model weights. To have a clean comparison, we evaluate TTME and TTT under the same discovery framework, replacing only the test-time adaptation method.  Our evaluation shows that TTME outperforms TTT on all five mathematical tasks, while reducing computational cost by 82.8-84.6% in FLOPs and 47.7-58.4% in runtime. These results establish TTME as an effective and computationally efficient alternative to TTT in the evaluated discovery settings.

title: VibeVideoBench: Evaluating Multimodal Agents on Code-Driven Video Generation

details.title: VibeVideoBench: Evaluating Multimodal Agents on Code-Driven Video Generation
details.abstract: 🎬 VibeVideoBench: Can AI agents make a finished video, entirely with code? Agents writing code to make videos is a new way to generate video 💡: multimodal agents write code to render every frame and synthesize every sound, so formulas, charts and narration timed to on-screen events come out exact. Meet VibeVideoBench 🚀, to our knowledge the first benchmark of general multimodal agents on open-domain, code-driven video generation with audio. 📦 The benchmark • 239 self-contained tasks in English and Chinese across 12 categories: data stories, music-driven pieces, classroom lessons, paper explainers, games, build-and-process videos and more • Agents run fully autonomously in their native harness, in a sandbox with no image or video generation model, only TTS • Deliver a finished MP4 with sound within one hour ⏱️ 🔍 Evaluation: hierarchical and evidence-based • L1 program checks of the delivery spec ✅ • L2 ~13k task-specific rubric checks, each traced to the requirement it enforces 📋 • L3 five quality dimensions, anchored per task 🎯 • Three independent VLM judge panels; audio checks only go to judges that can hear 👂 📊 Key findings (9 frontier agent systems, 2,151 scored rollouts) 🥇 GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5 rank 1st and 2nd with both the judges and blind human raters 🧩 Far from solved: the best system meets every core requirement on only 76.3% of tasks 📦 Delivery is a second axis: counting missing videos as zero reshuffles the ranking. Gemini 4 Argon delivers 77% of its videos and drops from 4th to 7th ⏰ Of 224 runs with no playable video, 169 are final renders that started too late, ran too slowly or never started. The problem is how agents plan their hour 🛠️ Every system keeps its own rendering stack; 95% of runs inspect their own frames, yet how much they look doesn't predict quality (ρ = −0.07) ⚖️ The judges rank systems like humans do (ρ = 0.98) but agree on only 73% of individual pairs: good for ranking systems, not single videos 🌐 Project page: https://vibevideobench.github.io/

title: LociArt: A Unified Paradigm for Free-Style Local Video Stylization

details.title: LociArt: A Unified Paradigm for Free-Style Local Video Stylization
details.abstract: A very interesting work on controllable video stylization. LociArt unifies region selection and style specification through polar style-aware masks, while its geometry-aware conditioning helps preserve boundaries and non-target content. The ability to compose multiple styles across regions without compositional training pairs makes the framework particularly promising for practical creative applications.

title: Zooming without Zooming v2: From Seeing Details to Connecting Evidence for Generalizable Multimodal Perception

details.title: Zooming without Zooming v2: From Seeing Details to Connecting Evidence for Generalizable Multimodal Perception
details.abstract: Recent multimodal models struggle with tasks that require connecting visual evidence across objects, images, and interactions, while collecting targeted supervision remains costly. We present Zooming-without-Zooming-v2 (ZwZ2) , a family of 4B/9B/27B models trained to connect evidence through reinforcement learning. Our EvidenceConnect framework uses privileged regional views to synthesize compositional questions, with cross-model agreement and region-ablation checks assessing label reliability and evidence dependence. Trained only on single-image questions and requiring no inference-time zooming, ZwZ2 improves over its base models on all 25 benchmarks across six domains , generalizing to multimodal long-context understanding, embodied spatial reasoning, and agents. We release all three models, the training dataset, and code. GitHub: https://github.com/inclusionAI/Zooming-without-Zooming-v2 Hugging Face collection: https://huggingface.co/collections/inclusionAI/zooming-without-zooming-v2

title: RSI Arena: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement with Human Feedback

details.title: RSI Arena: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement with Human Feedback
details.abstract: Can AI agents autonomously train useful language models and improve them using feedback from users? We introduce RSI Arena, a two-stage study of autonomous post-training as a step toward recursive self-improvement. Ten frontier models act as training agents, each starting from NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning 30B-A3B Base. During a six-day first stage, each agent has 1,000 GPU-hours and $300 in API credit on a shared 64-GPU cluster, independently selecting data, implementing training procedures, and choosing checkpoints. We evaluate their models on 20 benchmarks and through blind human evaluations. All ten agents produce working assistants, with the strongest model, trained by GPT-6 Astra, closing a median of 76% of the base-to-Instruct gap across 12 capability benchmarks. Its human-preference rating is also close to NVIDIA Instruct after statistical adjustment for answer length and formatting. In Stage 2, each agent receives the comparison records and votes involving its Stage 1 model and is given three additional days for further training. Using NVIDIA Instruct as a common reference across the two evaluation rounds, we observe an improvement from Stage 1 to Stage 2 in the style-adjusted relative rating of eight of the ten models. We show that benchmark gains were modest, with no clear link to preference gains, while some agents encouraged longer responses and one model showed increased harmful compliance on StrongREJECT. RSI Arena provides an auditable setting for studying how human feedback can guide autonomous model development. It takes a step toward recursive self-improvement with human feedback (RSIHF), in which people help define what improvement means for the AI systems they use.

title: RynnWorld-Latent: A Cross-Embodiment World Model Conditioned on Universal Latent Actions

details.title: RynnWorld-Latent: A Cross-Embodiment World Model Conditioned on Universal Latent Actions
details.abstract: Our main contributions are as follows: We present RynnWorld-Latent, a text-free, latent-action-conditioned video world model, which uses frozen RynnLAM descriptors as a shared conditioning interface for learning visual dynamics from human interaction videos, heterogeneous robot demonstrations, and simulation rollouts without aligning their native control spaces. We design an action-conditioning mechanism that combines global action tokens with locally identity-initialized, frame-aligned injection, associating transition descriptors with the corresponding future video latents. We enable latent-action-guided generation under edited robot embodiments and environments, and adapt the world model to native robot-action conditioning. The resulting latent-action synthesis and digital-teleoperation pipelines generate data that improves downstream policy learning in the evaluated settings.

Plus, it's fun to explore how cross-modal steering manifests in pixels and words Fantastic effort led by Donghao Zeng and awesome co-authors Nishant Subramani & Tamar Rott Shaham

title: What Effort Level Should I Choose? On the Economics of Reasoning Effort in LLM Agents

details.title: What Effort Level Should I Choose? On the Economics of Reasoning Effort in LLM Agents
details.abstract: Generative models increasingly expose a reasoning effort setting that lets users scale inference-time compute, trading higher cost for potentially improved performance. Users must choose an effort level before knowing whether extra reasoning will help, and even a successful run does not reveal whether the effort purchased was necessary. Reasoning effort is therefore a credence good: buyers observe the outcome but cannot assess the marginal value of the computation they paid for. In this work, we measure the counterfactual effect of effort levels on both proprietary and open-weight models on four benchmarks, spanning single-call reasoning and long-horizon agentic tasks. Effort, it turns out, does not consistently preserve tasks that lower effort solves, can overspend, and can change trajectory behavior. First, we find that although higher effort can raise accuracy in aggregate, it frequently fails on tasks that lower effort solved. Second, on the subset of easy tasks that every effort level solves, higher effort is generally more costly, with the highest effort level costing up to 42x as much as the lowest. Lastly, effort changes not only how many tokens are used, but also how agents solve tasks: at higher effort, agents verify their own work more heavily and more often search for solutions than work through problems directly, both of which lengthen trajectories without necessarily altering the outcome. These findings show that naively choosing the highest level is not only cost-inefficient but also offers no guarantee of the best instance-level performance. A simple alternative, starting at the lowest effort and escalating only after a verified failure, matches or improves on fixed top effort across all models and benchmarks at lower cost for most proprietary models.

title: The Lexical Imprint of Pre-training Data

details.title: The Lexical Imprint of Pre-training Data
details.abstract: 🎯 What traces does pre-training data leave on a language model? We've just arXived our NeurIPS 2026 paper, The Lexical Imprint of Pre-training Data! In this work, we explore how pre-training data shapes zero-shot behavior through word-level unigram cross-entropy, a simple, model-free measure of lexical alignment between pre-training corpora and target benchmarks. Perhaps unsurprisingly, we find that nearly all vocabulary in standard benchmarks is already covered during pre-training, given the billions of tokens used to train LLMs. What matters is not simply which words a model has seen, but how probability mass is distributed across them. This distribution leaves a measurable lexical imprint on the model's predictive behavior. Across controlled from-scratch experiments, we find that stronger lexical alignment consistently tracks higher zero-shot accuracy. #NeurIPS2026 #Pretraining #LLM #NAVER #KAIST_AI

title: On the SPOT: Enhancing Speculative Decoding for Diffusion Language Models via Commit-Order Prediction

details.title: On the SPOT: Enhancing Speculative Decoding for Diffusion Language Models via Commit-Order Prediction
details.abstract: Diffusion LMs already know most of the next tokens. What they miss is the order. SPOT learns it. Exact decoding of a diffusion LM fills one masked position per pass. The model's predictions from the previous pass already give the right token at over 90% of positions, but not which position comes next. SPOT is a 0.62M-parameter drafter that predicts this order from the target's own output distributions. The target checks a whole tree of candidates in one forward pass, and coupled-noise match keeps the output exact at any temperature. Up to 6.8× fewer target passes and up to 3.4× the throughput of standard decoding on SDAR-8B Matches or beats calibrated and training-free drafting baselines in every task and budget, at T = 0 and T = 1 The learned drafter transfers across six diffusion LMs New in v2, SPOT-Sets drafts whole commit sets for dynamic threshold decoding. Its exact mode keeps the threshold decoder's output and reaches 7.6× the throughput of standard decoding on SDAR-8B, against 5.0× for the threshold decoder alone (7.9× with max-commit) Code, drafters and a Colab demo are open. title: Learning and Reasoning with Geometry: How Generation Helps Spatial Understanding

details.title: Learning and Reasoning with Geometry: How Generation Helps Spatial Understanding
details.abstract: Image and video generators can produce spatially consistent visual content, but how to use this capability to improve spatial understanding remains underexplored. We study this problem from two perspectives: geometric supervision during training and explicit geometric evidence during inference. To this end, we introduce a unified geometric understanding and generation model (GeoUG) that integrates depth and multi-view generation with spatial understanding. First, we design a multi-scale depth codec that enables metric-depth generation using a pretrained visual autoencoder, and show that joint training yields task-dependent gains in spatial understanding. Second, we introduce 3DCueBench to control geometric difficulty while balancing selected 2D cues, and find that generated depth provides larger reasoning gains on questions requiring fine-grained geometric discrimination. Building on this finding, we develop adaptive interleaved reasoning, in which GeoUG first drafts an answer and then decides whether to generate geometric evidence to confirm or revise it. We train this decision through reinforcement learning, balancing accuracy gains over retaining the draft against generation cost. GeoUG achieves circular accuracies of 97.9%, 90.8%, and 94.2% on CV-Bench-3D, 3DCueBench, and DA-2K with fewer generation calls than always generating.

title: Rare, Relevant, and Still Wrong: How Memory Fails LLM Group Decisions

details.title: Rare, Relevant, and Still Wrong: How Memory Fails LLM Group Decisions
details.abstract: Can remembering more information actually make an LLM group worse at making decisions? In our new preprint, Rare, Relevant, and Still Wrong: How Memory Fails LLM Group Decisions , we investigate a fundamental question in multi-agent AI: what information should survive when a group's discussion is compressed into memory? Across four evaluated language models, we find that: Selecting relevant information can preserve misleading decoys. Prioritizing rare information is not consistently better than random selection. Facts attributed to multiple agents can receive undue weight, even when that apparent consensus provides no additional evidence. These findings suggest that better collective decision-making requires more than retrieving relevant information or preserving minority knowledge. How evidence is selected, represented, and attributed matters. We'd welcome feedback, alternative explanations, and discussion from researchers working on multi-agent systems, collective intelligence, and LLM memory.

title: Harness-Model Collaboration for Long-Horizon Continual Learning

details.title: Harness-Model Collaboration for Long-Horizon Continual Learning
details.abstract: We propose HaMo, a Harness-Model collaborative framework for continual learning in long-horizon agents. Our method separates adaptation into two tightly coupled processes. At the harness level, each trajectory is distilled into a compact experience card containing the task context, initial conditions, and a strategy-level solution outline. These cards are stored in a persistent non-parametric memory, making newly acquired procedural knowledge immediately available to future tasks. At the model level, HaMo continually updates a single parameter-efficient adapter using selected trajectories together with historical replay, improving the model’s ability to exploit accumulated experience while preserving previously acquired capabilities.

title: Multiscale Policy Optimization for Long-Horizon LLM Agents

details.title: Multiscale Policy Optimization for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
details.abstract: Excited to share Multiscale Policy Optimization (MPO), a reinforcement learning framework designed for long-horizon LLM agents! We observe that critic values vary primarily across assistant turns, motivating turn-level optimization with fine-grained token credit assignment. MPO combines Multiscale Advantage Estimation (MAE) with turn-level importance sampling to better align credit assignment and policy updates. Experiments on search, tool-use, and automation tasks with 4B and 30B-A3B models demonstrate consistent improvements over strong RL baselines.

title: h1: A Taste of the Bitter Lesson in Automated Theorem Proving

details.title: h1: A Taste of the Bitter Lesson in Automated Theorem Proving
details.abstract: While progress in informal mathematics has come largely from scaling the chain-of-thought and agentic reasoning of frontier language models, formal theorem proving has increasingly relied on human-designed workflows around these models, such as planning, decomposition, and orchestrating specialized provers. This raises a bitter-lesson question: can a simple agentic loop that scales test-time compute match these workflows? The answer matters as formal verification must scale to keep up with frontier models producing research mathematics, yet new workflows rarely settle it, as their gains are often confounded with stronger models or more compute. We study this question with h1, a simple harness that gives a model an efficient interface to Lean 4 and keeps it working through verifier feedback and self-reflection, without imposing a decomposition or search structure. h1 reaches state-of-the-art results on PutnamBench, FATE-X, and FormalConjectures100-Solved, settles eight open problems in FormalConjectures, and, at matched models, matches or outperforms specialized workflows such as Goedel-Architect and AlphaProof Nexus, surprisingly showing that a single attempt (pass@1) can often scale to solve open problems. Through ablations and matched-model comparisons with Claude Code and AxProverBase, we find that simplicity alone is not enough: an efficient Lean interface largely determines cost and solve rate. We thus recommend that future work evaluate frontier models with efficient execution feedback before prescribing workflows, at the risk of bitter lessons.

title: PhysEvolve: Verifier-grounded Self-evolution for Physical Reasoning with Executable Worlds

details.title: PhysEvolve: Verifier-grounded Self-evolution for Physical Reasoning with Executable Worlds
details.abstract: Physical reasoning underpins how embodied systems understand and act in the physical world, yet vision-language models (VLMs) remain unreliable on questions about dynamics and physical causality. Progress is critically constrained by the scarcity of grounded counterfactual training data, as observational videos capture only the factual trajectory that occurred. The self-evolving paradigm offers a route beyond fixed datasets by enabling models to construct their own training problems. Extending this paradigm to physics, however, requires an external source of truth that can both validate model-proposed environments and verify alternative physical outcomes under intervention. We introduce \physevolve{}, a verifier-grounded self-evolving framework that trains VLMs for causal physical reasoning from model-proposed executable worlds and simulation-authored tasks. At each round, a shared VLM proposes executable world programs and evidence schemas; a deterministic physics engine freezes each valid world, simulates matched baseline and body-elided counterfactual branches, and synthesizes discrete, answer-bound visual tasks. Exact verifier feedback from task solving updates both the shared policy via GRPO and an adaptive curriculum over physical intents. Starting from Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct, \physevolve{} achieves targeted gains across PhysBench, CausalPhys, and ContPhy without human intervention data, improving PhysBench Throwing by $8.8$ points and ContPhy Counterfactual Removal and Goal-Pit by $7.4$ and $24.4$ points. These gains concentrate on interaction-sensitive and altered-world questions, demonstrating zero-shot transfer of causal principles to unseen complex dynamics (cloth, fluid, soft bodies) and real-world video.

title: DTCA: Denoising Token Credit Assignment for Reinforcement Learning in Diffusion Language Models

details.title: DTCA: Denoising Token Credit Assignment for Reinforcement Learning in Diffusion Language Models
details.abstract: Which tokens contribute most to a diffusion language model’s response? As tokens are revealed during denoising, they help shape predictions at the remaining masked positions. However, final-answer rewards provide little information about these individual contributions. People often prioritize major word classes such as nouns and verbs when thinking about a topic, and diffusion language models may show a similar pattern with different POS contributing unequally. DTCA thus derives POS-based token-level credit from confidence gains during denoising, so that learning signals reflect each token’s estimated contribution to the rest of the response.

title: Efficient Streaming Audio-Visual Target Speaker Extraction for Real-World Acoustic Scenes

details.title: Efficient Streaming Audio-Visual Target Speaker Extraction for Real-World Acoustic Scenes
details.abstract: Falcon is a causal audio-visual target speaker extraction model that uses the target speaker's mouth video to extract their voice from noisy, overlapping speech. It combines a single-pass multi-scale time-frequency separator with an encoder-space speaker contrastive loss that reduces interfering-speaker leakage without adding inference cost. The paper also introduces RealSSA, a benchmark covering varied speaker counts, near- and far-field interference, reverberation, and sudden noise, with both simulated scenes and a held-out real-recorded evaluation set. Compared with causal AV-TFGridNet, Falcon reduces trainable parameters by 91.9%, computation by 20.2×, and GPU inference latency by 11.1× in the reported evaluation. Code, model weights, datasets, and interactive demos are available on the project page.

title: OmniShowcase: Omnidirectional Subject-Consistent Video Generation from Multi-View Images

details.title: OmniShowcase: Omnidirectional Subject-Consistent Video Generation from Multi-View Images
details.abstract: OmniShowcase: Omnidirectional Subject-Consistent Video Generation from Multi-View Images What OmniShowcase offers: 🔄 Every side, consistently: Generate videos of a subject from just 4 reference images , keeping identity and 3D shape consistent even through full 360° orbits . 🏭 3D-consistent data pipeline: Render the subject from one 3D asset along 88 camera trajectories and inpaint only the background, so unseen sides are never hallucinated. 📐 Geometry-aware conditioning: Feed the video model a surface-normal turntable reconstructed from the references, with no frame-wise alignment and no per-subject optimization. 📊 Results: Roughly halve geometric error vs. the best multi-view baseline on both ShowcaseBench and real-world NAVI objects ( −52% / −46% ). 📦 Open resources: Showcase-4K (4,000 training videos), ShowcaseBench (with GT meshes & cameras), and the code will be publicly released. 🌐 Project page: https://justin4ai.github.io/OmniShowcase/ 💻 Code: https://github.com/justin4ai/OmniShowcase 📄 Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.35684 Feedback and questions are very welcome!

title: Sensorimotor Alignment: A Platonic Proxy for Embodied Policy Success

details.title: Sensorimotor Alignment: A Platonic Proxy for Embodied Policy Success
details.abstract: The Platonic Representation Hypothesis (Huh et al, 2024) argues that as vision and language models scale, their representation spaces converge toward a shared statistical model of reality. The idea is that images and text are different projections of the same underlying world. As models recover that world more faithfully, they begin to agree on which inputs are similar. For example, if a vision model places two images close together in the representation space, a language model tends to place their captions close together too. In this work, we bring PRH to robotics and ask: can physical robot motion be viewed as another projection of that same world, such that more capable embodied models better align their vision and language representations with the structure of motion trajectories? Our evidence suggests the answer is yes. To test this, we use Sensorimotor Alignment (S²), which measures the overlap between neighborhoods of a model's sensory representations and neighborhoods of end-effector trajectories. Higher alignment means episodes nearby in sensory representation space are also nearby in motor representation space. Our first finding is that S² is positively related to downstream robot task success. We test a range of Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs) and World Action Models (WAMs) in simulation, as well as policies on real robots. Across these settings, models with higher S² tend to achieve higher task success rates. This pattern provides empirical support for extending PRH to robotics. S² also explains, at the representation level, several phenomena that prior work has observed only through closed-loop results. For example, VLAs often ignore the language instruction and act mainly on what they see. We find that their task success correlates with the S² of their vision features, not their text features. In practice, S² can serve as a low-cost offline proxy for identifying which models are likely to achieve higher task success before closed-loop evaluation. For instance, it can identify promising vision-language model (VLM) backbones even before costly VLA fine-tuning.

title: TAO: Tool-Aware Joint Scheduling for LLM-Based Agentic Serving

details.title: TAO: Tool-Aware Joint Scheduling for LLM-Based Agentic Serving
details.abstract: DeepInfer recently open-sourced how DeepSeek manages the KV cache with 3FS and balances prefill and decode loads. Since some of those load balancers remain unreleased, they propose their own effective router, TAO—a tool-aware joint scheduling framework designed for bursty agentic workloads under tight KV cache budgets. Targeting agentic workloads that alternate between clustered GPUs and distributed CPU tools, TAO improves scheduling in three steps: Tool-Boundary Interruption: Pauses sessions during external tool calls to free up GPU capacity and places them into a shared waiting pool. Triplet Session Valuation: Scores each session–node pair without manual weight tuning by prioritizing time-decayed KV-cache credit, near-term tool-return readiness (predicted from runtime hints and historical tool durations), and token footprint. Joint DP Placement: Replaces greedy per-session routing with an asynchronous dynamic program (under 0.12% runtime overhead) that jointly selects and places waiting sessions under GPU capacity limits. Tested on DeepSeek-V4 Flash, Qwen3-32B, and GLM-4.7, TAO cuts latency by up to 26.8%, lowers mean TTFT by up to 36.3%, and boosts decode throughput by up to 29.5% over leading baselines.

title: TauIndianBankBench: Procedure-Aware, Action-Oriented Evaluation of Tool-Using Conversational Agents

details.title: TauIndianBankBench: Procedure-Aware, Action-Oriented Evaluation of Tool-Using Conversational Agents
details.abstract: Hi everyone, author here! 👋 Thanks for checking out TauIndianBankBench . TL;DR: Most agent benchmarks only check the final database state. But many required banking steps, like getting a closure quote before closing a deposit, don't change any records, so an agent can skip them and still be marked successful. TauIndianBankBench has 1,000 Indian retail-banking tasks with a simulated customer. It scores the outcome , and it also checks that the agent completed every required step and made no unrequested changes . With outcome-only scoring, 6.5–12.0% of sessions across all models were counted as successes even though the agent broke the procedure. 📄 Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30161 📂 Dataset: https://huggingface.co/datasets/NPCI/tau-indian-banking 💻 Code: https://github.com/npci/TauIndianBankBench Contributions are welcome, whether that's new tasks, procedure fixes or additional banking flows. Feel free to open a PR on the dataset repo. You're also welcome to evaluate your own models and share the results. If you find this work useful, please upvote the paper and ❤️ like the dataset. It helps more people discover it! Happy to answer any questions! 🙏

title: CausGround: Causal Interaction Grounding for Adaptive Embodied Planning

details.title: CausGround: Causal Interaction Grounding for Adaptive Embodied Planning
details.abstract: CausGround: Causal Interaction Grounding for Adaptive Embodied Planning Embodied planning requires more than knowing what to do. Agents must also understand when an action is executable and how it changes the world. We introduce CausGround , a non-parametric causal interaction grounding framework that distills interaction experience into reusable action preconditions and effects, enabling adaptive embodied planning without updating model parameters. What CausGround offers: Learning causal knowledge from experience: CausGround extracts action preconditions and effects from interaction trajectories, organizing them into reusable generic and instance-specific knowledge. Factorized world-state representation: Object attributes and inter-object relations are explicitly represented, enabling causal knowledge to be grounded in current visual observations. Task-grounded causal planning: CausGround reasons backward over action preconditions and forward over action effects, guiding a frozen MLLM planner toward executable multi-step actions. Improved embodied planning: Across VirtualHome and RoboCasa, CausGround improves average task success from 24.9% to 53.3% and closed-loop planning success from 43.0% to 57.0% , respectively. Generalization across environments: CausGround improves interaction reasoning on SWITCH (25.8% to 31.9%) and demonstrates real-world sequential robotic manipulation without parameter updates. Toward continuously adaptable embodied agents: As new interaction experience becomes available, CausGround provides a way to expand reusable causal knowledge without retraining the underlying MLLM. Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.29702 Project Page: https://causground.github.io/ Code: https://github.com/Intelligent-Interaction/CausGround

title: HuGe: Scaling Humanoid Generalist Vision-Language-Action Models with Egocentric Experience

details.title: HuGe: Scaling Humanoid Generalist Vision-Language-Action Models with Egocentric Experience
details.abstract: HuGe (Humanoid Generalist) is a family of vision-language-action models for humanoid whole-body control. This repository provides Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct implementations of OFT-, GR00T-, and Pi-style policies that predict SONIC motion tokens and hand-control signals through a three-stage training pipeline: egocentric pre-training, humanoid adaptation, and downstream fine-tuning.

title: OmniSpectra: A Unified Foundation Model for Universal Spectra Representation Learning

details.title: OmniSpectra: A Unified Foundation Model for Universal Spectra Representation Learning
details.abstract: Hi everyone! Co-author here 👋 Spectra from different instruments sample the same wavelengths on very different pixel grids (up to 25× apart in our training corpus). Standard sequence models position tokens by pixel index, so the same line (e.g. Hα) gets a different positional code on every instrument. The usual fix is to resample everything onto a common grid, which blurs narrow lines. OmniSpectra is a wavelength-native masked autoencoder that removes this mismatch: Position = log λ, not pixel index. Tokens are anchored to physical wavelength. In log space, cosmological redshift becomes one uniform shift, which cancels in continuous RoPE, so attention depends on physical wavelength ratios rather than the detector grid. Resolution-gated Fourier decoder. Reconstructs flux at each instrument's native wavelengths. A gate set by the instrument's line-spread function suppresses detail the spectrograph cannot actually resolve. One set of weights, no resampling. Pretrained on 6.4M spectra from 8 surveys (SDSS, BOSS, eBOSS, SEGUE-1/2, DESI, APOGEE, GALAH). With only 12.2M parameters , it reaches state-of-the-art results across stellar parameters, galaxy properties, source classification and redshift, and outperforms much larger models such as AstroCLIP and AION-1. It is especially strong when labels are scarce. Pretrained on SDSS alone, it still transfers to APOGEE, whose near-infrared range it never saw during pretraining, with little degradation. Happy to answer questions!

title: Intrinsic Distribution Matching

details.title: Intrinsic Distribution Matching
details.abstract: Hi everyone! We’re excited to share IDM: Intrinsic Distribution Matching . Can a generator provide both the score supervision and the representation used for distribution matching? Building on internal DMD, IDM retains the full DMD correction and adds an explicit loss on the means and per-coordinate standard deviations of the generator’s own EMA features , without an external feature encoder. A Gaussian-plus-residual decomposition of the reverse-KL field motivates this additional moment constraint. At 2 NFE , IDM (Z-Image) achieves 94.25% on LongText-CN and 90.20% on LongText-EN , the best scores among the compared methods at this budget. Controlled ablations show consistent gains from the added moment loss, while generator EMA features perform competitively with DINOv2. We evaluate both Z-Image-Turbo 6B and Qwen-Image 20B with full-parameter and LoRA tuning. Model weights: coming soon. If you find the work interesting, we’d appreciate a GitHub star ⭐ and an HF upvote!

title: Your Benchmark Is an Empirical Measure Over Difficulty

details.title: Your Benchmark Is an Empirical Measure Over Difficulty
details.abstract: The paper views a benchmark as an empirical measure over difficulty, which enables it to formalize measure mismatch and coverage gaps and derive theoretical results and practical diagnostics. The paper further introduces BenchFill, a difficulty-targeted rewriting method that augments benchmarks by generating new examples in underrepresented difficulty regions to reduce coverage gaps.

title: Look Only When Needed: Certificate-Guided Visual Routing for Efficient Diffusion VLMs

details.title: Look Only When Needed: Certificate-Guided Visual Routing for Efficient Diffusion VLMs
details.abstract: LOWN (Look Only When Needed) is a training-free decoding method for diffusion vision-language models (DVLMs) that processes the image only when a text-only prediction disagrees with the last image-conditioned prediction. Diffusion VLMs such as LLaDA-V process the whole image at every denoising step, but we find that removing the image changes a token being unmasked at only 22.8% of steps on average. Agreement certifies the earlier prediction for reuse, and the number of certified tokens sets how many are unmasked in that step. Without training or a tuned threshold, LOWN retains 99.6% of LLaDA-V's score on ten benchmarks at 35.3% of the decoding FLOPs and cuts generation time by 57.4% on average. Project page: https://hyeon9698.github.io/LOWN/ Code: https://github.com/hyeon9698/LOWN

title: WorkFactory: Turning Professional Intents into Executable Work for Scalable Agent Training

details.title: WorkFactory: Turning Professional Intents into Executable Work for Scalable Agent Training
details.abstract: Excited to share WorkFactory, a scalable framework for synthesizing coherent and executable professional tasks to train Working Agents! WorkFactory combines professional intent synthesis, information support graphs, and execution-guided repair to construct high-quality tasks that enable reliable expert demonstrations. We build 112,686 tasks spanning 612 occupations and train the WorkPilot model family at 4B, 27B, and 35B-A3B scales. All three models achieve consistent improvements across four professional-work benchmarks, with WorkPilot-35B-A3B improving from 879 to 1565 Elo on GDPval-AA v2.1. We hope this work contributes to scaling general-purpose agents for real-world professional tasks!

title: A Broader Look into MLLM's Retrieval Heads

details.title: A Broader Look into MLLM's Retrieval Heads
details.abstract: We study how omni-modal LLMs retrieve relevant evidence, focusing on how retrieval mechanisms extend from text and vision to audio-visual inputs. Across 18 model checkpoints, including eight omni-modal models, we find that retrieval relies on a sparse set of attention heads that are largely preserved from language or vision-language backbones. By presenting the same evidence as speech or on-screen text, we show that audio and visual retrieval largely recruit the same heads. Ablating the shared subset, comprising fewer than 2% of all attention heads, also degrades document understanding, spatial perception, and visual mathematics, revealing its role in broader multimodal capabilities. Building on these findings, we optimize retrieval-head attention with a ranking objective for document retrieval, improving Qwen3-VL-8B’s page Recall@1 on MMDocIR by 6.03 percentage points over the untrained scorer, with gains across three model families.

title: Co-Design Bench: Multimodal Collaborative Coding Evaluation for Agentic Models

details.title: Co-Design Bench: Multimodal Collaborative Coding Evaluation for Agentic Models
details.abstract: Can a coding agent turn a real user's multimodal request into a complete, working application revision? We're sharing Co-Design Bench: Multimodal Collaborative Coding Evaluation for Agentic Models , a benchmark built around real users' requests to revise existing applications. Each task starts with a runnable application and asks the agent to understand the user's intent, make the necessary changes, and satisfy every acceptance criterion. Real requests, multimodal inputs, and connected changes. Co-Design Bench contains 273 tasks and 2,331 expert-authored acceptance criteria , curated from 37,463 deduplicated queries across 26,314 real user coding sessions . It covers two complementary tracks: Multimodal Editing (100 tasks): localized revisions grounded in annotated screenshots and optional image, audio, video, or document inputs. Repository Editing (173 tasks): coordinated changes across components, routes, state, data flow, and content. Requests can involve reproducing distinct text animations from a video, correcting a dashboard from a receipt and updating its dependent totals, or coordinating layout and interaction changes across an application. Tasks span Grounded Understanding, UI Transformation, and Functional Implementation , often combining several capabilities within one request. Evaluate the running application, with evidence for each requirement. Our reference-free judge-then-refute protocol assesses hidden acceptance criteria using source code and browser evidence. A separate verifier challenges positive judgments for stubs, hardcoded outputs, unreachable functionality, and requirement mismatches. Evidence audits require screenshots for visual claims and recorded browser actions for interaction claims. No gold implementation or target screenshot is required. Partial requirement satisfaction and complete delivery tell different stories. Across 10 model endpoints under a shared agentic harness , the strongest endpoint, gpt-6-astra , passes an average of 69.9% of criteria per task , yet fully satisfies only 26.4% of tasks . All ten endpoints achieve lower criterion completion on repository requests spanning three or four edit types than on those spanning one or two. Qwen3.8-27B reaches 64.4% overall strict completion , ranking fourth overall, and 64.5% on Repository Editing , ranking second on that track in this evaluation. It also leads the text-only Multimodal Editing subset at 77.9% . Rankings vary with the editing setting; the small repository-track score differences do not establish a general model advantage. The ME-96 subset comprises 96 Multimodal Editing tasks and 521 acceptance criteria , a distinct scope from the full 273-task paper evaluation. Explore the real cases, demonstrations, evaluation tools, and results: Project & demos · Paper · Code & evaluation · Dataset We welcome researchers and builders working on coding agents, multimodal grounding, and reliable application editing to try the benchmark and share their findings!

title: VibeGame: Prompt-to-Game Development with AI-Native Engine and Self-Evolving Adversarial Agent Team

details.title: VibeGame: Prompt-to-Game Development with AI-Native Engine and Self-Evolving Adversarial Agent Team
details.abstract: Excited to share VibeGame, a framework that turns prompts (text and optional reference images) into complete, playable 2D game projects! To let agents build a complete, vivid game with no given assets, we build an AI-native game engine that agents can read and control frame by frame. On top of it, a self-evolving team of eight agents designs the game, creates its own art and animations, writes the code, and plays and reviews the result until it passes. On 30 GameCraft-Bench tasks, VibeGame outperforms the strongest baseline harness by 11.70 points with GPT-5.6-Luna and by 4.19 points with GPT-6.1-Sol.

title: Read, Allocate, Route: Role-Coupled Tokenization for Pixel-Space Generative Transformers

details.title: Read, Allocate, Route: Role-Coupled Tokenization for Pixel-Space Generative Transformers
details.abstract: We introduce SpecSlot, a role-coupled tokenization method for pixel-space generative Transformers. SpecSlot decouples fine visual detail from global communication by assigning tokens fixed spectral output roles: low-frequency carriers perform global attention, while the remaining slots interact locally. On ImageNet-512, SpecSlot-K4 uses 38.2% fewer FLOPs than JiT-B/16. For 256×256 text-to-image generation, it reduces forward compute from 218.77 to 129.86 GFLOPs while improving DPG-Bench from 61.15 to 62.21. Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.40647 Project Page: https://yangjiongfan.site/specslot/ Code: https://github.com/JiongfanYang/SpecSlot

details.title: CoSTA: Compressed Speech Token Adaptation for Efficient Spoken Dialogue Models

title: Glance: The Generator Is Its Own Reranker

details.title: Glance: The Generator Is Its Own Reranker
details.abstract: Glance: one model. Judge, rank, generate. RAG usually serves two models: a cross-encoder reranker that encodes every (query, passage) pair, then a generator that reads the winners again. We show the generator can be its own reranker. All k passages are prefilled once into a shared state, one short probe per passage continues from that cache, and a LoRA + pointer head scores every passage in the same pass. With the adapter off, the same weights chat as usual. On a 9B hybrid (Gated DeltaNet) backbone: 39 min of training on one B200: SciFact nDCG@10 0.741, NFCorpus 0.345 (bge-reranker-v2-m3: 0.721 / 0.326) Scales to k=200 candidates: 0.717 vs 0.659 for BGE (SciFact subset) HotpotQA answer F1 +0.045 over BGE-selected context, same generator (paired bootstrap CI excludes 0) Activated variant: chat stays bit-identical to the base model, and the answer continues the reranking cache Adapters + code (Apache-2.0): https://huggingface.co/airun-ai/GlanceRAG-MiMo-9B-Reranker

title: AskStream: When and What to Ask Proactively under Uncertainty in Streaming Video Understanding

details.title: AskStream: When and What to Ask Proactively under Uncertainty in Streaming Video Understanding
details.abstract: Recent advances in multimodal large language models have increased interest in interaction paradigms for video understanding. The evolution from offline to streaming and proactive interaction has gradually shifted models from passive responders toward more proactive agents that can decide when to answer. However, existing proactive paradigms typically assume that the information required to answer a query is complete, leaving models to only wait or answer. In the real world, however, information is often incomplete due to uncertainty from either the video or the user. In proactive paradigms, such uncertainty can cause the model to wait forever or generate highly hallucinatory responses. We therefore argue that proactive interaction should be redefined with a third action: ask, allowing models to actively ask for missing information. To study when and what models should ask before answering, we introduce AskStream, the first multi-turn benchmark spanning video and user uncertainty for streaming video understanding, with four task categories and eight subtasks. It contains 438 videos with 2,714 manually annotated frame-level time windows across three types: wait, ask, and answer. Across both multiple-choice and open-ended settings, even the strongest model attains only 52.18% on our proposed Ask-F1 metric, highlighting substantial limitations in proactive information seeking under uncertainty.

title: Investor's Last Exam: Can AI Agents Do Equity Investment Without Seeing the Future?

details.title: Investor's Last Exam: Can AI Agents Do Equity Investment Without Seeing the Future?
details.abstract: Evaluating forecasting capability usually means waiting for outcomes to materialize — months, sometimes years — during which market conditions, fundamentals, and the information environment shift enough that scores can no longer be cleanly attributed to the model; moreover, most work in LLM4Finance has focused on the research stage rather than the investment stage, which is where the field's core objective lies. ILE asks whether an agent, using only what was visible at decision time, can independently complete the full chain from evidence to assumptions to forecast. To answer it, we built a versioned corpus (3.43M document versions, 1.52TB, 9 source classes) that enforces the cutoff across the entire toolchain — specify a timestamp and you get exactly the versions visible at that moment — and organized 86 assignments around buy-side analyst deliverables, with rubrics anchored to sources and reproducible calculations through financial dependency graphs. Among current SOTA systems, Astra scores 78.9 on Research & Evidence but only 52.5 on Forecast & Model, and ordering by realized outcomes puts DeepSeek V4.1 Flash ahead (40.3 vs 37.7): today's models are very good at organizing evidence of what has already happened into coherent analysis, and not yet good at turning that analysis into judgment about what has not. For me, the longer-term significance is on the training side — once the time boundary is a mechanism, historical timestamps become a re-samplable environment for large-scale domain RL, with evaluation and training sharing one environment.

details.abstract: We show the standard multi-token prediction (MTP) gradient hides a KL self-distillation gradient signal behind a noisy residual, and introduce the KL gradient–recovery trick to extract it. This is a free lunch that improves MTP across a range of tasks.

title: Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities

details.title: Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities
details.abstract: Youtu-Parsing-Omni is a compact (5B) omni-modal parsing model. Given a single input — a document page, a natural image, a chart / flowchart, a geometry figure, an audio clip or an audio-visual video — it produces one structured JSON envelope that covers both perception (layout elements, text, tables, formulas, bounding boxes, timestamps, ASR, OCR, acoustic events, camera motion) and cognition (captions, narratives, reports). Input --task modality / subtype Key contents Document page document image / document layout elements with bbox, text / LaTeX / OTSL tables / Markdown charts / Mermaid flowcharts, reading order Natural image natural_image image / natural_image entities and text with bbox, tags, captions, global description Chart graphics_chart image / document one chart element: Markdown table, notes, caption Flowchart graphics_flowchart image / document one flowchart element: Mermaid, caption Geometry figure graphics_geometric image / document one geometric element: points, lines, arcs, shapes, geometric relations and measurements Audio audio audio / – vocal / non-vocal segments with timestamps, speakers, ASR, timbre / scene captions, acoustic events Natural video natural_video video / natural_video temporal segments with visual elements, actions, interactions, camera motion, audio track Text-rich video textrich_video video / text_rich_video segments with OCR + ASR and a Markdown structured_report of the whole video Highlights: Unified schema – one JSON envelope for seven parsing families, driven by the task prompt. Omni encoder – image, audio and interleaved audio-visual video inputs (frames + audio track) in a single model. Strong results at a small size – state-of-the-art on OmniDocBench v1.6 (96.96 Overall), best open-weight model on OmniParsingBench (75.08 Avg., second only to Gemini-3-Pro), and competitive with specialized models on chemical-structure (ChemOCR) and music-score (PDMX-Synth) recognition ( results ). Easy to serve – a vLLM plugin, pinned serving settings, task prompts and inference examples are included.

title: Online Dense Reinforcement Learning with Planning-Grounding Agent for UI Navigation on Live IOS Apps

details.title: Online Dense Reinforcement Learning with Planning-Grounding Agent for UI Navigation on Live IOS Apps
details.abstract: While frontier vision-language models demonstrate strong capabilities in user interface (UI) navigation, their high inference costs prohibit everyday use. Conversely, smaller models trained via supervised fine-tuning (SFT) or offline reinforcement learning often memorize static trajectories, leading to brittle execution and an inability to recover from errors. To address these limitations, we propose a novel online reinforcement learning framework that trains UI navigation agents directly on live iOS applications. Our framework decouples the agent into two specialized components: a Planning agent and a UI Grounding model. We rely on an LLM-as-a-Judge to provide comprehensive reward signals, combining dense, step-level feedback to evaluate intermediate progress with a terminal reward for overall task completion. To effectively leverage this dual reward structure, we optimize the agent using Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) with step-level advantage estimation. Furthermore, we introduce GiGPPO, a novel neighbor-conditioned value estimation method that improves critic stability by leveraging reward signals from visually similar states across concurrent trajectories. To support this online training paradigm at scale, we introduce an efficient infrastructure that orchestrates hundreds of concurrent virtual iOS devices. Evaluations on rigorous benchmarks, including UINavBench, iOSWorld, and AndroidWorld, demonstrate that our online RL trained agents substantially outperform both SFT and terminal-only RL baselines while accelerating training convergence. Notably, our 8B RL agents achieve nearly a sevenfold improvement over the SFT baseline in out-of-distribution generalization to Android environments, while outperforming Gemini-3.5-Flash and tying with Gemini-3.1-Pro on real iOS applications.

title: Your LR Schedule May Not Be Principled: Effective Learning Rate Scheduling in Weight-Normalized Training

details.title: Your LR Schedule May Not Be Principled: Effective Learning Rate Scheduling in Weight-Normalized Training
details.abstract: Weight-normalized (WN) training is emerging as a compelling alternative to conventional weight decay (WD), with recent studies reporting substantial pretraining loss gains. We show that these gains are driven primarily by the induced effective learning rate (ELR) trajectory rather than by normalization alone. Matching ELR trajectories largely collapses the training loss dynamics of WN and WD. Schedule design should therefore target ELR rather than the nominal learning rate (LR) alone. Building on this principle, we propose AIR ( A ffine I nverse-square- R oot decay), which combines a theoretically derived $1/\sqrt{t}$ decay with an affine adjustment to satisfy prescribed peak and terminal LRs over a finite training horizon. We further identify late-stage ELR scheduling as a key source of its gains, because a shared late schedule attenuates the effect of earlier LR choices. Experiments on 128 B-token Mixture-of-Experts pretraining demonstrate that AIR outperforms cosine and other candidate schedules in training loss, downstream performance, and hyperparameter robustness, reducing terminal training loss by approximately 0.01 relative to cosine at matched cumulative LR. Applying the same ELR trajectory to WD reproduces the corresponding training dynamics, showing that the benefits extend beyond fixed-norm training and establishing ELR as the principled scheduling object.

title: After One-Click Video: The Inflow of Service-Type Content, the Failure of the Recommendation Pool Mechanism, and the BoLe System

details.title: After One-Click Video: The Inflow of Service-Type Content, the Failure of the Recommendation Pool Mechanism, and the BoLe System
details.abstract: One-click video tools now let anyone make good-looking content fast. Most of it is service-type content: people watch it to meet a need, not to enjoy the content itself. Before competing, creators, tool builders and model researchers should first ask which kind they are making, because the two kinds win by different rules. Our paper draws this line, and uses a simple model to show why the free platform’s trial-viewing pool stops working when service-type content keeps pouring in. Try the demo: set AI output to 100x and watch one year.

title: Holo4D: Holistic 4D Reconstruction as Geometric Control for Video Diffusion

details.title: Holo4D: Holistic 4D Reconstruction as Geometric Control for Video Diffusion
details.abstract: Excited to share Holo4D, accepted to NeurIPS 2026! 🎥 Give it a video and a new camera path, and Holo4D reshoots the video from that camera. It lifts the source video into 3D tracks (a 4D scaffold) and uses them to steer a pretrained video diffusion model: the tracks keep what the camera saw in place, and the video model fills in what it never saw. Works with different 4D reconstructors without retraining, so it improves as 4D reconstruction improves Reshoots real robot videos (DROID arms, humanoids), although Holo4D itself is trained without robot videos Extends to longer videos window by window Everything is open: code (training and inference), 14B / 5B checkpoints, evaluation code, and the predictions behind every table. 🌐 Project: https://nirvanalan.github.io/projects/holo4d/ 💻 Code: https://github.com/NIRVANALAN/Holo4D 🤗 Models: https://huggingface.co/yslan/Holo4D-2026

title: FDSML: Formula-Driven Supervised Metric Learning with Parameter-Aware Triplet Loss

details.title: FDSML: Formula-Driven Supervised Metric Learning with Parameter-Aware Triplet Loss
details.abstract: FDSML pre-trains vision models without real images, using the generating formula itself as supervision: fractals with more similar parameters should lie closer in the embedding space. We turn this parameter-space ordering into triplets, so the model learns how images relate to each other.

title: Intrinsic Distribution Matching

details.title: Intrinsic Distribution Matching
details.abstract: Hi everyone! We’re excited to share IDM: Intrinsic Distribution Matching . Can a generator provide both the score supervision and the representation used for distribution matching? Building on internal DMD, IDM retains the full DMD correction and adds an explicit loss on the means and per-coordinate standard deviations of the generator’s own EMA features , without an external feature encoder. A Gaussian-plus-residual decomposition of the reverse-KL field motivates this additional moment constraint. At 2 NFE , IDM (Z-Image) achieves 94.25% on LongText-CN and 90.20% on LongText-EN , the best scores among the compared methods at this budget. Controlled ablations show consistent gains from the added moment loss, while generator EMA features perform competitively with DINOv2. We evaluate both Z-Image-Turbo 6B and Qwen-Image 20B with full-parameter and LoRA tuning. Model weights: coming soon. If you find the work interesting, we’d appreciate a GitHub star ⭐ and an HF upvote!

title: Your Benchmark Is an Empirical Measure Over Difficulty

details.title: Your Benchmark Is an Empirical Measure Over Difficulty
details.abstract: The paper views a benchmark as an empirical measure over difficulty, which enables it to formalize measure mismatch and coverage gaps and derive theoretical results and practical diagnostics. The paper further introduces BenchFill, a difficulty-targeted rewriting method that augments benchmarks by generating new examples in underrepresented difficulty regions to reduce coverage gaps.

title: Look Only When Needed: Certificate-Guided Visual Routing for Efficient Diffusion VLMs

details.title: Look Only When Needed: Certificate-Guided Visual Routing for Efficient Diffusion VLMs
details.abstract: LOWN (Look Only When Needed) is a training-free decoding method for diffusion vision-language models (DVLMs) that processes the image only when a text-only prediction disagrees with the last image-conditioned prediction. Diffusion VLMs such as LLaDA-V process the whole image at every denoising step, but we find that removing the image changes a token being unmasked at only 22.8% of steps on average. Agreement certifies the earlier prediction for reuse, and the number of certified tokens sets how many are unmasked in that step. Without training or a tuned threshold, LOWN retains 99.6% of LLaDA-V's score on ten benchmarks at 35.3% of the decoding FLOPs and cuts generation time by 57.4% on average. Project page: https://hyeon9698.github.io/LOWN/ Code: https://github.com/hyeon9698/LOWN

title: Proving and Improving the Platonic Representation Hypothesis with JEPAs

details.title: Proving and Improving the Platonic Representation Hypothesis with JEPAs
details.abstract: Authors here 👋 We prove the Platonic Representation Hypothesis for JEPAs: with good views (two observations of one scene), encoders trained separately on any modalities learn the same representation, up to one rotation. Next-token prediction is a JEPA with bad views, so LLMs align with vision only through scale. Our 109M good-view text JEPA scores .184 on the PRH benchmark, above Qwen2.5-72B (.154) and Llama-3-70B (.151), and needs 42× fewer samples than next-token prediction on the same texts. 🤗 Demo, caption your own photos and videos (no network trained on image–caption pairs; one rotation fitted on pairs): https://huggingface.co/spaces/galilai-group/prh_demo 💻 Code: https://github.com/galilai-group/prh-proof

title: Read, Allocate, Route: Role-Coupled Tokenization for Pixel-Space Generative Transformers

details.title: Read, Allocate, Route: Role-Coupled Tokenization for Pixel-Space Generative Transformers
details.abstract: We introduce SpecSlot, a role-coupled tokenization method for pixel-space generative Transformers. SpecSlot decouples fine visual detail from global communication by assigning tokens fixed spectral output roles: low-frequency carriers perform global attention, while the remaining slots interact locally. On ImageNet-512, SpecSlot-K4 uses 38.2% fewer FLOPs than JiT-B/16. For 256×256 text-to-image generation, it reduces forward compute from 218.77 to 129.86 GFLOPs while improving DPG-Bench from 61.15 to 62.21. Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.40647 Project Page: https://yangjiongfan.site/specslot/ Code: https://github.com/JiongfanYang/SpecSlot

title: WorkFactory: Turning Professional Intents into Executable Work for Scalable Agent Training

details.title: WorkFactory: Turning Professional Intents into Executable Work for Scalable Agent Training
details.abstract: Excited to share WorkFactory, a scalable framework for synthesizing coherent and executable professional tasks to train Working Agents! WorkFactory combines professional intent synthesis, information support graphs, and execution-guided repair to construct high-quality tasks that enable reliable expert demonstrations. We build 112,686 tasks spanning 612 occupations and train the WorkPilot model family at 4B, 27B, and 35B-A3B scales. All three models achieve consistent improvements across four professional-work benchmarks, with WorkPilot-35B-A3B improving from 879 to 1565 Elo on GDPval-AA v2.1. We hope this work contributes to scaling general-purpose agents for real-world professional tasks!

title: A Broader Look into MLLM's Retrieval Heads

details.title: A Broader Look into MLLM's Retrieval Heads
details.abstract: We study how omni-modal LLMs retrieve relevant evidence, focusing on how retrieval mechanisms extend from text and vision to audio-visual inputs. Across 18 model checkpoints, including eight omni-modal models, we find that retrieval relies on a sparse set of attention heads that are largely preserved from language or vision-language backbones. By presenting the same evidence as speech or on-screen text, we show that audio and visual retrieval largely recruit the same heads. Ablating the shared subset, comprising fewer than 2% of all attention heads, also degrades document understanding, spatial perception, and visual mathematics, revealing its role in broader multimodal capabilities. Building on these findings, we optimize retrieval-head attention with a ranking objective for document retrieval, improving Qwen3-VL-8B’s page Recall@1 on MMDocIR by 6.03 percentage points over the untrained scorer, with gains across three model families.

title: VibeGame: Prompt-to-Game Development with AI-Native Engine and Self-Evolving Adversarial Agent Team

details.title: VibeGame: Prompt-to-Game Development with AI-Native Engine and Self-Evolving Adversarial Agent Team
details.abstract: Excited to share VibeGame, a framework that turns prompts (text and optional reference images) into complete, playable 2D game projects! To let agents build a complete, vivid game with no given assets, we build an AI-native game engine that agents can read and control frame by frame. On top of it, a self-evolving team of eight agents designs the game, creates its own art and animations, writes the code, and plays and reviews the result until it passes. On 30 GameCraft-Bench tasks, VibeGame outperforms the strongest baseline harness by 11.70 points with GPT-5.6-Luna and by 4.19 points with GPT-6.1-Sol.

title: Co-Design Bench: Multimodal Collaborative Coding Evaluation for Agentic Models

details.title: Co-Design Bench: Multimodal Collaborative Coding Evaluation for Agentic Models
details.abstract: Can a coding agent turn a real user's multimodal request into a complete, working application revision? We're sharing Co-Design Bench: Multimodal Collaborative Coding Evaluation for Agentic Models , a benchmark built around real users' requests to revise existing applications. Each task starts with a runnable application and asks the agent to understand the user's intent, make the necessary changes, and satisfy every acceptance criterion. Real requests, multimodal inputs, and connected changes. Co-Design Bench contains 273 tasks and 2,331 expert-authored acceptance criteria , curated from 37,463 deduplicated queries across 26,314 real user coding sessions . It covers two complementary tracks: Multimodal Editing (100 tasks): localized revisions grounded in annotated screenshots and optional image, audio, video, or document inputs. Repository Editing (173 tasks): coordinated changes across components, routes, state, data flow, and content. Requests can involve reproducing distinct text animations from a video, correcting a dashboard from a receipt and updating its dependent totals, or coordinating layout and interaction changes across an application. Tasks span Grounded Understanding, UI Transformation, and Functional Implementation , often combining several capabilities within one request. Evaluate the running application, with evidence for each requirement. Our reference-free judge-then-refute protocol assesses hidden acceptance criteria using source code and browser evidence. A separate verifier challenges positive judgments for stubs, hardcoded outputs, unreachable functionality, and requirement mismatches. Evidence audits require screenshots for visual claims and recorded browser actions for interaction claims. No gold implementation or target screenshot is required. Partial requirement satisfaction and complete delivery tell different stories. Across 10 model endpoints under a shared agentic harness , the strongest endpoint, gpt-6-astra , passes an average of 69.9% of criteria per task , yet fully satisfies only 26.4% of tasks . All ten endpoints achieve lower criterion completion on repository requests spanning three or four edit types than on those spanning one or two. Qwen3.8-27B reaches 64.4% overall strict completion , ranking fourth overall, and 64.5% on Repository Editing , ranking second on that track in this evaluation. It also leads the text-only Multimodal Editing subset at 77.9% . Rankings vary with the editing setting; the small repository-track score differences do not establish a general model advantage. The ME-96 subset comprises 96 Multimodal Editing tasks and 521 acceptance criteria , a distinct scope from the full 273-task paper evaluation. Explore the real cases, demonstrations, evaluation tools, and results: Project & demos · Paper · Code & evaluation · Dataset We welcome researchers and builders working on coding agents, multimodal grounding, and reliable application editing to try the benchmark and share their findings!

title: CoSTA: Compressed Speech Token Adaptation for Efficient Spoken Dialogue Models

details.title: CoSTA: Compressed Speech Token Adaptation for Efficient Spoken Dialogue Models
